statement: The band and its canonical decompositions: Put \[ \Gamma=W(p)=\{\lambda\in\overline\Q^{\times}:\ p^N\lambda\text{ is integral for some }N\geq0, \quad |\tau\lambda|=p^{w(\lambda)/2}\ (\tau),\quad w(\lambda)\in\Z\}. \] Then $G=D(\Gamma)$, where $D$ is the contravariant equivalence from Galois modules to groups of multiplicative type. Let $\mu_\infty$ be the group of roots of unity, $\Gamma^0=\ker(w)$, and $M=\Gamma^0/\mu_\infty$. There are canonical identifications \begin{align*} X^*(G^0)&=\Gamma/\mu_\infty=M\oplus\Z[\sqrt p],\\ G/G^0&=\widehat\Z,\qquad G^0=H^0\times\Gm, \qquad H^0=D(M),\\ X^*(H)&=\Gamma'=\Gamma/\langle\mu_\infty,p\rangle =M\oplus\Z/2\Z,\\ H&=H^0\times\mu_2. \end{align*} The maps $\epsilon:G\to\Gm$ and $i:\Gm\to G$ have character maps $1\mapsto p$ and $\lambda\mapsto w(\lambda)$, respectively, and $\epsilon i(t)=t^2$. The restriction $i|_{\mu_2}$ splits $H$. The group $M$ is a $\Q$-vector space, and complex conjugation acts as $-1$. Consequently $H^0$ is a protorus, an inverse limit of tori compact at the real place. It is not an algebraic torus of finite type.
status: Proved under the stated Tate hypothesis; the group calculation is unconditional

statement: The transcription is not a group definition: The transcription of 15:5 reads ``entiers alg\'ebriques'' and ``$\nu\in\mathbf Z^+$''. Those elements form a monoid, not the character group of a rigid category: $p$ is in it and $p^{-1}$ is not. We have explicitly replaced that text by its group of fractions. Both positive and negative integral weights occur. Weight zero does not imply root of unity once denominators at $p$ are allowed. Also the arrow transcribed as $i|_{\mu_2}:\mu_2\to H^0$ must land in $H$; its composite with $H\to\mu_2$ is the identity, so it cannot land in $H^0$.

statement: Artin versus Artin--Tate rigidification: Let $F^0$ be the intrinsic fibre functor on $\operatorname{Niv}^0(\mathcal M)^0$, the Artin motives. The gerbe of fibre functors extending this $F^0$, with an identification on that subcategory, has band $G^0$, not $H$. To obtain band $H$ one must also fix a trivialization of the Tate line. Equivalently one extends $F^0$ to the Artin--Tate subcategory by $F^0(\Q(1))=\Q$. Its group is \[ G/H=D(\mu_\infty\oplus\Z p) =\widehat\Z\times\Gm. \]

statement: Geometric base change and the universal Frobenius: There is a canonical isomorphism \[ \Gamma/\mu_\infty\xrightarrow{\sim} W(p^\infty):=\varinjlim_{n\mid n'} \bigl(W(p^n),\lambda\mapsto\lambda^{n'/n}\bigr). \] Thus $G^0=P$, the Weil-number protorus of Langlands--Rapoport and Milne, and $H^0=P_0$, its weight-zero factor. The base-change functor $\mathcal M_p\to\mathcal M_{\overline{\F}_p}$ induces the inclusion $P\hookrightarrow G$ on bands. The inclusion $\Gamma\hookrightarrow\overline\Q^\times$ is Galois equivariant and hence defines a canonical $\mathfrak f\in G(\Q)$.

statement: Centres and crystalline endomorphisms: For a simple $N\in\mathcal M_q$ the algebra $A_N=\End(N)$ is a central division algebra over $E_N=\Q[\mathfrak f_N]$, and \[ A_N\otimes\Q_p\simeq \End_{F\text{-}\mathrm{Isoc}(\F_q)}(T_pN). \] The right side means endomorphisms commuting with crystalline Frobenius, including its semilinear structure. It does not mean all endomorphisms of the underlying vector space. If $d_N^2=[A_N:E_N]$, then $\operatorname{rank}(N)=d_N[E_N:\Q]$.

statement: The warning about $\Z$ and $\widehat\Z$: Over $\F_p$, an isocrystal is a finite-dimensional $\Q_p$-vector space with an invertible \emph{linear} operator. Forgetting the operator is an exact faithful tensor functor to $\Q_p$-vector spaces. Thus $T_p$, after this forgetting, really is a fibre functor over $\Q_p$. Its Frobenius action generally does not extend continuously from $\Z$ to $\widehat\Z$. Over $\overline{\F}_p$ the realization instead takes values in the $\Q_p$-linear category $\mathcal R_p$ of isocrystals on $B=W(\overline{\F}_p)[1/p]$. Its fibre-functor gerbe has band $D(\Q)$ and class $\beta_p$ characterized by \[ \operatorname{inv}_p\bigl(s_*(\beta_p)\bigr)=s\pmod\Z, \qquad s\in\Q=X^*(D(\Q)). \] It is not neutral over $\Q_p$.
status: Proved; Lead A2 is false in its proposed nonneutral interpretation over $\F_p$
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The Artin torsor and the connecting map: For the Artin--Tate rigidification of Proposition~\ref{A:rigidification}, let $\eta_p=\operatorname{Isom}^{\otimes}(T_p|_{\mathrm{Artin}},F^0_p)$, with the right action on the source; extend it by the trivial Tate factor. Under \[ H^1(\Q_p,G/H)=H^1(\Q_p,\widehat\Z) =\Hom_{\rm cts}(G_{\Q_p},\widehat\Z), \] it is the unramified quotient. Arithmetic local Frobenius maps to $+1$ when the canonical motivic Frobenius is the generator $+1$. The opposite isomorphism torsor has value $-1$ and gives $\xi_p=-\partial(\eta_p^{\mathrm{op}})$ instead. The class of the rigidified gerbe is \[ \xi_p=\partial(\eta_p),\qquad \partial:H^1(\Q_p,G/H)\longrightarrow H^2(\Q_p,H). \]
status: Proved under the stated Tate hypothesis; the Artin calculation is unconditional
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The real obstruction, with the Serre argument repaired: The full category over $\F_p$ has no $\R$-valued fibre functor. At infinity the rigidified gerbe has class \[ \xi_\infty=(0,1/2)\in H^2(\R,H^0)\times H^2(\R,\mu_2)=0\times\Z/2\Z. \] The nonzero class is represented by the real Weil extension, whose lift $j$ of complex conjugation satisfies $j^2=-1$.
status: Proved for abelian motives, and hence under the stated hypothesis for all motives
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Compact real tori satisfy the degree-two Hasse principle: If $T/\Q$ is a torus compact over $\R$, with character lattice $L$, then $\Sha^2(\Q,T)=0$. In fact \[ H^2(\Q,T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_v H^2(\Q_v,T). \]
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The global class really is locally determined: For $H^0=D(M)$ one has \[ \Sha^2(\Q,H^0)=0,\qquad H^2(\R,H^0)=0. \] For a finite place $v$, there is a canonical identification \[ H^2(\Q_v,H^0)=\Hom\bigl(M^{G_{\Q_v}},\Q/\Z\bigr). \] More precisely, for any cofinal countable increasing sequence of Galois-stable lattices $L_n\subset M$, and $T_n=D(L_n)$, \[ H^2(\Q,H^0)=\varprojlim_n H^2(\Q,T_n) =\varprojlim_n\bigoplus_v H^2(\Q_v,T_n). \] These equalities are conclusions of the proof, not definitions of cohomology. The assertion in A.3 that $\Sha^2$ of an arbitrary protorus is simply a limit of finite-level $\Sha^2$ is not a valid general rule.
status: Proved unconditionally for the band in Theorem~\ref{A:band}
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Explicit global and local classes: Write $v_p(p)=1$, and for $m\in M$ choose a Weil-unit representative $u$. The number $v_p(m):=v_p(u)$ is independent of that choice. There is exactly one class \[ \xi_0=(a_p,b_{p,\infty})\in H^2(\Q,H^0)\times H^2(\Q,\mu_2) \] with local components \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{lll} \toprule Place & $H^0$ component & $\mu_2$ component\\ \midrule $\ell\ne p,\infty$ & $0$ & $0$\\ $p$ & $m\mapsto v_p(m)\pmod\Z$, $m\in M^{G_{\Q_p}}$ & $1/2$\\ $\infty$ & $0$ & $1/2$\\ \bottomrule \end{tabular} \end{center} Here $b_{p,\infty}$ is the quaternion Brauer class ramified exactly at $p$ and infinity, viewed in $H^2(\Q,\mu_2)$ by Kummer. The compact component $a_p$ has infinite order. The finite local components determine both factors of $\xi_0$.
status: Proved unconditionally for the constructed gerbe; motivic identification under the stated hypotheses
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: An explicit arithmetic description of the character module: For finite Galois CM fields $K\subset\overline\Q$, let $X_K$ be their sets of primes above $p$. Then \[ M\simeq\varinjlim_K \{f:X_K\to\Q:\ f(cw)=-f(w)\}, \] where transition maps pull back functions along maps of primes, and $[u]$ maps to $w\mapsto\operatorname{ord}_w(u)/ \operatorname{ord}_w(p)$. In particular the local groups and the functional in Theorem~\ref{A:class} are specified by explicit rational permutation modules.
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The correct comparison, and the strict-band counterexample: Let $\mathscr H$ be the Artin--Tate rigidified gerbe of class $\xi_0$. Its pushout along $H\hookrightarrow P=G^0$ is the pseudomotivic $P$-gerbe of \citet[Theorem 3.29 and Theorem 3.31]{AMilne1994}, with the inverse-limit and adelic corrections of \citet[Theorem 6.3 and Definition 6.6]{AMilne2003}. Equivalently it is the gerbe obtained by rigidifying only the Artin fibre functor $F^0$, and under the motivic hypotheses it is the gerbe of motives over $\overline{\F}_p$. There is no band-preserving equivalence of the $H$-gerbe itself or of the full $G$-gerbe with that $P$-gerbe. Their bands have component groups $\mu_2$, $\widehat\Z$, and $1$, respectively. The morphisms that do exist are pushouts \[ \mathscr H\longrightarrow\mathscr P \longrightarrow\mathscr G, \qquad H\hookrightarrow P\hookrightarrow G. \]

notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Dictionary between gerbes and groupoids: Let $\mathscr P$ be a $P$-gerbe over $\Q$ and choose $x\in\mathscr P(\overline\Q)$. Its groupoid over $\Spec(\overline\Q)\times_{\Spec\Q}\Spec(\overline\Q)$ is the sheaf of isomorphisms between the two pullbacks of $x$. Its diagonal kernel is $P_{\overline\Q}$. For each place $v$, a realization functor induces a morphism of such groupoids; its map on kernels is $1\to P_{\Q_\ell}$ for $\ell\ne p$, $D(\Q)\to P_{\Q_p}$ at $p$, and $\Gm\to P_\R$ at infinity. Conversely fpqc descent for this groupoid recovers $\mathscr P$. Changing $x$ changes the groupoid by an isomorphism whose conjugacy ambiguity is exactly the change of the chosen identification of objects.
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Unconditional $H$-gerbe and its automorphisms: The class in Theorem~\ref{A:class} defines an $H$-gerbe over $\Q$ with exactly the prescribed local classes. It is unique up to $H$-equivalence. No nonzero class can be added without changing some local class. The group of isomorphism classes of its band-preserving self-equivalences is \[ H^1(\Q,H)=\Q^\times/\Q^{\times2}\times \frac{\prod_n T_n(\Q)} {\{(a_n f_n(a_{n+1})^{-1})_n:(a_n)_n\in\prod_nT_n(\Q)\}}, \] for the explicit lattice exhaustion in Theorem~\ref{A:hasse}; $f_n:T_{n+1}\to T_n$ is its transition. The group of automorphisms of any one such equivalence is $H(\Q)=\{\pm1\}$.
status: Proved unconditionally as a statement about banded gerbes
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The bare category and the category with local data: Fix the band diagram $H\hookrightarrow G$, the grading $i$, and the augmentation $\varepsilon$, with the Artin--Tate rigidification specified in Proposition~\ref{A:rigidification}. Then $\xi_0$ determines the underlying Tannakian category with these structures up to compatible equivalence, and conversely. It does not in general determine a family of chosen local neutralizations extending the fixed rigidification. Write $S=\{\ell:\ell\ne p,\ \ell\text{ finite}\}$. The precise replacement for that stronger classification is relative cohomology, defined by the shifted cone of $R\Gamma(\Q,H)\to\prod_{\ell\in S}R\Gamma(\Q_\ell,H)$. For a fixed locally trivializable class its fibre is a torsor under \[ \coker\left[H^1(\Q,H)\longrightarrow \prod_{\ell\in S}H^1(\Q_\ell,H)\right]. \] The same statement with a restricted adelic product applies when an integral compatibility condition is imposed.
