notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Forgetting the local comparison framings: Fix the category and global Artin--Tate rigidification of Proposition~\ref{A:enrichment}. Suppose that the prime-to-$p$ realizations form one object over the finite adeles away from $p$, and that this adelic object's Artin restriction is isomorphic to $F^0\otimes\mathbb A_f^p$, not just separately at each place. At $p$ fix the Artin restriction of the ordinary crystalline $\Q_p$ fibre functor, namely the unramified Artin torsor computed in Proposition~\ref{A:eta}. If the local comparison isomorphisms with these restrictions are \emph{not} part of the data, all such coherent systems on the fixed gerbe are equivalent. One may also include the prescribed real realization morphism. Thus the underlying class suffices for the equivalence class of this unframed coherent system. This assertion and the framed counterexample in Proposition~\ref{A:enrichment} concern different specified data. The equivalence itself is not asserted to be unique as an equivalence preserving the global $H$-rigidification.
status: Proved for coherent adelic systems with the prescribed Artin restrictions
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: What the Lefschetz category actually supplies: Let $\operatorname{LMot}(\overline{\F}_p)$ be the category generated by abelian varieties, with correspondences generated by divisor classes and with the ordinary Tannakian commutativity constraint. It is a semisimple Tannakian category. Its band is \[ L=\mathop{\prod}_{\Pi}^{\Gm} L_\Pi,\qquad X^*(L_\Pi)=\Z^{\Pi}/ \{f:c f=f,\ \textstyle\sum_{\pi\in\Pi}f(\pi)=0\}, \] where $\Pi$ runs through the geometric simple isogeny classes, identified with Galois orbits of integral weight-one Weil germs. The fibre product identifies every multiplier $[\pi]+[c\pi]$. In particular $L$ is commutative, but it is not the Weil-number protorus $P$ in general. Compatible powers of Frobenius generate a subgroup $P\hookrightarrow L$. Prime-to-$p$ realization and crystalline realization, the weight and Tate morphisms, and the real obstruction are available unconditionally. The claimed identification of the entire character group with Weil numbers, full Frobenius-centralizer faithfulness for arbitrary tensor objects, and the resulting formula for $H^0$ cannot simply be transferred to this smaller-correspondence category.
status: Proved unconditionally; equality of its band with $P$ is refuted
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: An explicit extra Frobenius relation: Take $p=5$, $\alpha=1+2i$, and $\beta=(3+\sqrt{-11})/2$. They are Frobenius numbers of the elliptic curves \[ E_\alpha:y^2=x^3+x,\qquad E_\beta:y^2=x^3+4x+2 \quad\text{over }\F_5, \] which have four and three rational points, respectively. Choose $\lambda^2=\alpha\beta$. This is an integral weight-one $5$-Weil number, with irreducible polynomial \[ x^8-6x^6+15x^4-150x^2+625. \] Honda--Tate supplies a simple abelian fourfold $B/\F_5$ with this Frobenius number. In \[ h^1(B)^{\otimes2}\otimes h^1(E_\alpha)^\vee \otimes h^1(E_\beta)^\vee \] there is a geometric eigenline on which Frobenius is $1$, but the Lefschetz group acts nontrivially. Thus its character is zero on $P$ and nonzero on $L$.
status: Refuted: $L=P$ for all finite-field Lefschetz motives
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The unconditional gerbes used in Kisin's paper: Kisin's quasi-motivic gerbe has a band $Q$ defined by a universal condition on real and $p$-adic cocharacters. Its pushout by $Q\twoheadrightarrow P$ is the pseudomotivic gerbe, with the same $P$ and the same local realization morphisms as above. This construction is unconditional. It supplies a Tannakian category of representations of that gerbe; identifying that category with all numerical motives is a separate claim with the hypotheses of A.1. The quasi-motivic band $Q$ itself is not a replacement name for $G$, $H$, or $P$.
status: Known construction; the signed dictionary proved and independently checked
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: The literature date changes the abelian scope: The dated primary preprint of \citet[Theorem I]{AvanHoftenSempliner2026} proves the rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties. Its \S1.1.2--1.1.3 applies Milne's Hodge-to-Tate implication to all abelian varieties over finite fields. With these cited results the full-correspondence category of abelian motives, and all its tensor powers, has the Weil band $P$ unconditionally. This does not change the Lefschetz category: the latter was defined by restricting its morphisms to those generated by divisors, and Example~\ref{A:lefschetz-counterexample} still proves that its band can be larger. Nor does this theorem settle the Tate conjecture for arbitrary smooth projective varieties. The preprint status and exact version are retained in the bibliography rather than represented as an earlier theorem.
status: Known from the opened October 2026 theorem; the implication is stated explicitly
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Restriction on the arithmetic class: For \(k_m=\F_{q^m}\), restriction sends \[ e_q\longmapsto m e_{q^m}. \] For the point, Weil--etale motivic cohomology is \[ H^i_{\BW}(\Spec\F_q,\Z(n))= \begin{cases} \Z,&n=0,\ i=0,1,\\ \Z/(q^{|n|}-1),&n\ne0,\ i=1,\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}, \end{cases}\tag{B.1} \] where for negative twists the etale convention is \(\Z(n)=\Q/\Z'(n)[-1]\), with the characteristic-primary part omitted. After tensoring with \(\Q\), only the two groups with \(n=0\) survive.
notes: Negative twists use Q/Z prime-to-characteristic shifted by -1; l=p cyclotomic convention excluded.

statement: The precise comparison gate: Let \(X/\F_q\) be smooth and projective of dimension \(d\). In the notation of Geisser's Conjectures~8.1--8.3, let \(K(X,n)\) denote the integral Weil--etale to continuous-cohomology comparison, \(L(X,n)\) finite generation, and \(T(X,n)\) the conjunction of the Tate cycle-class conjecture in codimension \(n\), semisimplicity at eigenvalue one, and equality of rational and numerical equivalence in that codimension. Then \[ K(X,n)+K(X,d-n)\ \Longrightarrow\ L(X,n) \ \Longrightarrow\ K(X,n)\ \Longrightarrow\ T(X,n). \tag{B.2} \] Assuming \(T(Y,r)\) for every smooth projective variety over finite fields and every \(r\), all the comparisons \(K(X,n)\) and finite-generation statements \(L(X,n)\) follow. Moreover, independently of these conjectures, \[ H^i_{\BW}(X,\Q(n))\simeq H^i_{\BM}(X,\Q(n))\oplus H^{i-1}_{\BM}(X,\Q(n)). \tag{B.3} \] Cup product with \(e_q\) acts on these summands by \( (a,b)\mapsto(0,a)\).
notes: The literal continuity and algebraically closed vanishing requirements contradict the finite-point computation. The compatible universal comparison has exactly the numerical-Chow-phantom gate under Tate and semisimplicity. All abelian-type cases are proved using the current external CM Hodge theorem.; Universal three-part Geisser T implies comparison and finite generation.

statement: A contradiction already at the point: There is no cohomology theory which simultaneously has the finite-field Weil--etale value \(H^1(\F_q,\Q)=\Q e_q\), the restriction in Proposition~\ref{prop:B-e}, continuity under the filtered union of finite extensions, and vanishing of higher cohomology over \(\overline{\F}_q\).
notes: The direct limit of the degree-one rational lines is Q, not zero.

statement: All twists for motives of abelian type, using the current theorem: Let \(X/\F_q\) be smooth projective, and suppose that its rational Chow motive belongs to the thick rigid category generated by abelian varieties and Artin motives. Then, for every \(i,n\) and every prime \(\ell\), \[ H^i_{\BW}(X,\Z(n))\otimes\Z_\ell \xrightarrow{\sim}H^i_{\Bcts}(X,\Z_\ell(n)), \] and all the integral Weil--etale groups are finitely generated. For \(\ell=p\), the right side is the logarithmic Hodge--Witt comparison, rather than a cyclotomic etale sheaf in characteristic \(p\). In particular, \[ H^i_{\BW}(X,\Q(n))= \begin{cases} CH^n(X)_\Q,&i=2n,\ 2n+1,\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}, \end{cases} \] where cup product by the normalized \(e_q\) identifies the two copies. Thus the previously known divisor and curve cases extend to all twists on all abelian varieties, and on all varieties of abelian type. This statement does not assert that every Chow motive is of abelian type.
status: Proved from the cited current theorem
notes: Current CM Hodge theorem implies all-abelian Tate. Tate passes to abelian-type projectors; Kimura nilpotence supplies rational=numerical, so every integral comparison and finite generation follow, including logarithmic p-adic coefficients.

statement: The remaining universal assertion is exactly a phantom-motive gate: Assume Tate surjectivity and semisimplicity at eigenvalue one for every smooth projective variety over \(\F_q\), in every codimension. Then the following universal statements are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item The integral Weil--etale comparison holds for all varieties, degrees and twists, and all these integral groups are finitely generated. \item Rational equivalence equals numerical equivalence on all rational Chow groups. \item There is no nonzero rational Chow motive \(P\) whose image \(\bar P\) in numerical motives is zero. \item Every rational Chow motive belongs to the category generated by abelian and Artin motives. \end{enumerate} In particular, the missing assertion in B.1 can be expressed without an unspecified regulator or unspecified comparison map: it is the vanishing of numerical Chow phantoms. The Tate and semisimplicity hypotheses alone have not been shown to imply that vanishing here.
status: Proved equivalence; the equivalent universal assertion remains unresolved
notes: Explicit splitting M=N+P with N abelian-type and P numerical phantom; nilpotence on N corrects the lifted inverse. This is an exact remaining obstruction, not a proof phantoms vanish.

statement: All full rational etale groups, with the defect left visible: For every prime \(\ell\), \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} n&H^0_{\Bcts}(U,\Q_\ell(n))& \dim_{\Q_\ell}H^1_{\Bcts}(U,\Q_\ell(n))& \dim_{\Q_\ell}H^2_{\Bcts}(U,\Q_\ell(n))\\ \hline 0&\Q_\ell&r_2+1+\delta_{K,\ell}(0)&\delta_{K,\ell}(0)\\ 1&0&r_1+r_2-1+|T|&|T|-1\\ n\ge2&0&r_n&0\\ n<0&0&r_n+\delta_{K,\ell}(n)&\delta_{K,\ell}(n). \end{array}\tag{B.10} \] All other degrees vanish. For \(n=1\), more precisely, \[ H^1_{\Bcts}(U,\Q_\ell(1))= \mathcal O_{K,T}^\times\otimes\Q_\ell,\qquad H^2_{\Bcts}(U,\Q_\ell(1))= \ker\bigl(\Q_\ell^T\xrightarrow{\sum}\Q_\ell\bigr). \tag{B.11} \] For \(n\ge2\), the Chern-class map identifies degree one with \(K_{2n-1}(\mathcal O_K)^{(n)}\otimes\Q_\ell\). The defect \(\delta_{K,\ell}(0)\) is exactly the Leopoldt defect. For \(n<0\), writing \(m=1-n\), it is exactly the dimension of the kernel of the \(\ell\)-adic regulator \[ K_{2m-1}(\mathcal O_K)^{(m)}\otimes\Q_\ell \longrightarrow\bigoplus_{v\mid\ell}K_v .\tag{B.12} \] In particular, replacing every defect in (B.10) by zero is equivalent, at the indicated \((K,\ell,n)\), to Leopoldt for \(n=0\), or to Schneider's regulator-injectivity conjecture at \(m=1-n\) for \(n<0\).
notes: Negative-twist defect is strict positive-twist regulator kernel; no unproved vanishing asserted.

statement: An unconditional rational structure in degree one: For every integer \(n\), all primes \(\ell\), and the above geometric local conditions, the natural realization maps give \[ H^1_{f,X}(K,\Q_\ell(n))\simeq V_X(n)\otimes\Q_\ell, \quad V_X(n)= \begin{cases} \mathcal O_{K,S}^\times\otimes\Q,&n=1,\\ K_{2n-1}(\mathcal O_K)^{(n)}\otimes\Q,&n\ge2,\\ 0,&n\le0. \end{cases}\tag{B.15} \] In particular the degree-one assertion for negative twists does not require Schneider's conjecture. That conjecture concerns the full groups in (B.10), not the group in (B.15).
notes: S-units for n1, Adams K eigenspaces n>=2, zero n<=0.

statement: The common rational spaces in every Tate degree: For \(X=\Spec\mathcal O_{K,S}\), the following table lists all possibly nonzero common \(\Q\)-spaces \(H^i_{\rm abs}(X,\Q(n))\). The dual in the table is the \(\Q\)-linear dual. \[ \begin{array}{c|c|l} n&i&H^i_{\rm abs}(X,\Q(n))\\ \hline 0&0&\Q\\ 0&2&(\mathcal O_K^\times\otimes\Q)^\vee\\ 1&1&\mathcal O_{K,S}^\times\otimes\Q\\ 1&2&\ker(\Q^S\xrightarrow{\sum}\Q)\\ 1&3&\operatorname{coker}(\Q^S\xrightarrow{\sum}\Q)\\ n\ge2&1&K_{2n-1}(\mathcal O_K)^{(n)}\otimes\Q\\ n<0&2&(K_{1-2n}(\mathcal O_K)^{(1-n)}\otimes\Q)^\vee . \end{array} \tag{B.17a} \] Every unlisted group is zero. For every prime \(\ell\), including two, these spaces tensor to the cohomology of the specified Selmer complex with the geometric open-place conditions. Neither Leopoldt nor Schneider is assumed in this assertion.
status: Proved for the specified absolute and Selmer complexes
notes: Complete all-degree/all-twist Q table. Two Poitou-Tate exact sequences give degree2 through chosen splittings, not a claimed canonical derived duality. At removed places twist1 includes full local H2, yielding invariant kernel/cokernel.

statement: The exact support sequence and corank: There is an exact sequence \[ \begin{split} 0\longrightarrow\Sha(A/K)[\ell^\infty] \longrightarrow H^1_{\et}(X,A)[\ell^\infty] \longrightarrow\bigoplus_{v\mid N\ \mathrm{or}\ v\mid\infty} H^1(K_v,A)[\ell^\infty] \longrightarrow\mathcal S_\ell(A^t)^D . \end{split}\tag{B.19} \] There is no assertion of surjectivity onto the last term. Put \(d=[K:\Q]\dim A\), \(s=\Bcorank_{\Z_\ell}\Sha(A/K)[\ell^\infty]\), and let \[ t=\operatorname{rank}_{\Z_\ell}\operatorname{im} \left(\mathcal S_\ell(A^t)\longrightarrow \prod_{v\mid\ell}A^t(K_v)^{\wedge}_\ell\right). \] Then \[ \Bcorank_{\Z_\ell}H^1_{\et}(X,A)[\ell^\infty]=d+s-t. \tag{B.20} \] If \(\Sha(A/K)[\ell^\infty]\) is finite, then \(t\) is the dimension of the \(\ell\)-adic closure of the Mordell--Weil group \(A^t(K)\) inside its local points. It must not in general be replaced by the abstract rank \(r=\operatorname{rank}A(K)\).
notes: t is local closure rank of pro-Selmer, not abstract Mordell-Weil rank.

statement: The counterexample in R6, without a BSD assumption: Take \[ E=X_0(11):\quad y^2+y=x^3-x^2-10x-20. \] Its discriminant is \(-11^5\), its conductor is \(11\), and it has good reduction over \(\Z[1/11]\). The reproducible algebraic two-descent in \texttt{part\_b/code/x011.gp} gives \[ \operatorname{ellrank}(E)=[0,0,0,[]],\qquad E(\Q)_{\rm tors}\cong\Z/5, \] with torsion generator \((5,5)\). Thus its rank is certified to be zero; this uses no analytic-rank computation or BSD. PARI's official description of \texttt{ellrank} specifies that the lower and upper bounds and the two-descent data are unconditional. The model of \(X_0(11)\) is also derived explicitly in Elkies's October~13, 2021 lecture notes~\cite{BElkies2021,BPari2026}. For any prime \(\ell\), let \(X=\Spec\Z[1/(11\ell)]\). The Kummer sequence gives \[ 0\longrightarrow E(\Q)\otimes\Q_\ell \longrightarrow H^1_{\Bcts}(X,V_\ell E) \longrightarrow V_\ell H^1_{\et}(X,E)\longrightarrow0. \] The first term is zero. The global Euler characteristic of \(V_\ell E\), whose complex-conjugation eigenspaces both have dimension one, is \(-1\). Its \(H^0\) is zero, so \(\dim H^1=1+\dim H^2\ge1\). It follows that \(H^1_{\et}(X,E)[\ell^\infty]\) is infinite for every \(\ell\). For \(\ell=2\) the zero two-Selmer calculation additionally gives \(\Sha(E)[2]=0\), hence \(\Sha(E)[2^\infty]=0\); then (B.20) gives exact corank one. All hypotheses of the boxed assertion on 12:75 hold, including invertibility of \(\ell\) on \(X\), and its conclusion fails.
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: An arithmetic relative-curve counterexample to 12:79: Let \(S=\Spec\Z[1/22]\) and let \(f:X\to S\) be the smooth proper genus-one curve given by the above model of \(X_0(11)\), with its zero section. Then \[ \left(\Br(X)/f^*\Br(S)\right)[2^\infty] \simeq H^1_{\et}(S,E)[2^\infty] \] has \(\Z_2\)-corank one. Thus surjectivity modulo finite groups of \(\Br(S)\to\Br(X)\) is false for arithmetic bases, even for a smooth proper relative curve with a section.
notes: S=Z[1/22], X=E_S; quotient2-primary corank1. Primary decomposition of torsion quotient is explicitly justified.

statement: Splitting off divisor classes on a smooth open variety: Let \(Y/\F_q\) be smooth, separated and of finite type, and let \(N_Y\) be the image of \(\BPic(\bar Y)\otimes\Q_\ell\) in \(H^2(\bar Y,\Q_\ell(1))\), for \(\ell\ne p\). Then \(N_Y\) is a \(\Gamma\)-equivariant direct summand. No semisimplicity or Tate conjecture for the complementary summand is assumed.
notes: Unconditional; full Frobenius semisimplicity and Tate are not needed.

statement: The finite-field chain over a regular finite-type base: For the smooth separated base \(S\) above, the natural map \[ H^1(S,A)[\ell^\infty]\longrightarrow H^1(\bar S,\bar A)[\ell^\infty]^\Gamma \] has finite kernel and cokernel. Consequently the following four conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item \(H^1(S,A)[\ell^\infty]\) is finite; \item the Kummer map \(A(S)\otimes\Q_\ell\to H^1_{\Bcts}(S,V_\ell A)\) is an isomorphism; \item the same map to \(W^\Gamma\) is an isomorphism; \item \(H^1(\bar S,\bar A)[\ell^\infty]^\Gamma\) is finite. \end{enumerate} These are equivalences, without an assumption that their equivalent finiteness assertions hold. If \(S\) is projective and \(A\) is constant, these assertions of finiteness hold unconditionally.
notes: Algebraic divisor subspace splits on smooth open via Hodge index, weights, alteration trace. [a] eigenspace on total dual abelian scheme splits geometric Kummer; cofiniteness promotes rational isomorphism to finite kernel and cokernel.

statement: Relative curves without a section: Let \(S/\F_q\) be smooth, separated and connected of finite type, and let \(f:Y\to S\) be a smooth proper curve with geometrically connected fibres and relative Jacobian \(J\). For \(\ell\ne p\), \[ V_\ell\bigl(\Br(Y)/\operatorname{im}\Br(S)\bigr) \simeq V_\ell H^1(S,J). \tag{B.32} \] The kernel of \(\Br(S)[\ell^\infty]\to\Br(Y)[\ell^\infty]\) is finite. Consequently the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item \(\Br(S)\to\Br(Y)\) is surjective modulo a finite \(\ell\)-primary group; \item \(H^1(S,J)[\ell^\infty]\) is finite; \item \(H^1(\bar S,\bar J)[\ell^\infty]^\Gamma\) is finite. \end{enumerate} If \(f\) has a section, the natural edge map gives the stronger integral isomorphism \[ (\Br(Y)/\Br(S))[\ell^\infty] \simeq H^1(S,J)[\ell^\infty]. \]
notes: A Cartier closure supplies degree d, not a finite multisection. Rational Leray and Picard identify the quotient Tate module; cofinite torsion gives equivalence modulo finite groups.

statement: A source error avoided in the preceding proof: Keller's Lemma~2.17 claims that the closure of a generic-fibre point of a proper relative curve is finite over an integral base. This is false in the printed generality. Over any finite field take \(S=\mathbb A^2_{x,y}\), \(Y=\mathbb P^1_{[u:v]}\times S\), and the generic point \([u:v]=[x:y]\). Its closure is \(uy-vx=0\), the blowup of the origin, whose fibre over \((0,0)\) is the whole \(\mathbb P^1\). On its two standard charts the coordinate rings are \(k[x,t]\), \(y=xt\), and \(k[y,s]\), \(x=ys\); it is integral and has no additional irreducible component. This explicitly contradicts the lemma's quasi-finiteness step. The degree of the associated line bundle, which is all the proof above uses, remains one on every fibre. Thus the section-free part of the preceding proposition is not inherited from that lemma or from its use in Corollary~2.18 and Theorem~4.27~\cite[Lemma~2.17]{BKeller2016}.
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Sections and their completion on a reduced base: Let \(S/\F_q\) be reduced and of finite type, without a separatedness assumption, and let \(A/S\) be an abelian scheme. Put \(C_S=A(\bar S)\). Then \(C_S/(C_S)_{\rm tors}\) is finitely generated, its Galois action has finite image, and the natural map gives an isomorphism \[ C_S\otimes_{\Z}\Q_\ell \xrightarrow{\sim} (C_S)^{\wedge}_\ell\otimes_{\Z_\ell}\Q_\ell \qquad (\ell\ne p). \] There exists a finite disjoint union \(V\) of smooth separated finite-type \(\F_q\)-schemes with a jointly surjective map \(v:V\to S\). Pullback embeds \(C_S\) in \(C_V\) and embeds their quotients by torsion.
notes: Reduced-base section injection and LangNeron give finite free quotient; ell torsion embeds in finitely many Pruefer groups, so completion rationalization agrees with tensor Qell.

statement: The finite-field chain for arbitrary finite-type schemes: Let \(S/\F_q\) be any scheme of finite type, let \(A/S\) be an abelian scheme, and let \(\ell\ne p\), including \(\ell=2\) when \(p\ne2\). No regularity, reducedness, properness or separatedness of \(S\) is required. Set \[ W_S=H^1_{\Bcts}(\bar S,V_\ell A),\qquad N_S=A(\bar S)\otimes\Q_\ell. \] The geometric Kummer sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow N_S\longrightarrow W_S \longrightarrow V_\ell H^1_{\et}(\bar S,\bar A) \longrightarrow0 \] has a \(\Gamma\)-equivariant splitting. The natural map \[ H^1_{\et}(S,A)[\ell^\infty]\longrightarrow H^1_{\et}(\bar S,\bar A)[\ell^\infty]^\Gamma \] has finite kernel and cokernel. The four conditions in Proposition~\ref{prop:B-finite-chain-proper} are therefore equivalent for every such \(S\).
notes: Section space embeds in the finite-Galois section representation of a jointly surjective smooth alteration cover. Averaging a linear projection and composing its Kummer retraction proves the splitting without hypercover descent.

statement: Why the positive-degree argument retains its regularity hypothesis: There is a reduced projective surface \(S/\F_2\) and a smooth proper genus-one scheme \(f:X\to S\) for which every global line bundle has relative degree zero. Thus the positive-degree class used in Proposition~\ref{prop:B-relative-curve} cannot be asserted on an arbitrary singular base. This example does not assert that the Brauer quotient is infinite. Take \[ E:\ y^2z+yz^2+x^3+x^2z=0\ \subset T=\mathbf P^2_{\F_2}, \qquad O=[0:1:0], \qquad S=T\amalg_E T. \] The derivatives of the cubic are \(x^2,z^2,y^2+x^2\), with no common projective zero, so \(E\) is an elliptic curve. The pushout is the explicit finite \(T\)-scheme \[ S=\operatorname{Spec}_T(\mathcal O_T\oplus\mathcal O_T(-3)), \qquad R[t]/(t(t-f_E))\simeq R\times_{R/(f_E)}R \] on each trivializing affine, where multiplication on the second summand uses the cubic section \(f_E\). It is reduced because the displayed algebra embeds in the product of two domains, and projective because it is finite over \(T\). Let \(A=E\times S\). The closed-cover sequence on the small etale site is \[ 0\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow i_{1*}A_T\oplus i_{2*}A_T \xrightarrow{\mathrm{res}_1-\mathrm{res}_2}i_{E*}A_E \longrightarrow0. \] For surjectivity it suffices to pass to a strict henselian local ring. A section into the smooth curve \(E\) on its closed quotient lifts across the resulting henselian pair; see the Stacks Project, Lemma~15.13.3~\cite{BStacksSmoothLift}. The kernel is the fibre-product description of \(S\). Every map \(\mathbf P^2\to E\) is constant, since its restriction to each projective line is constant, whereas the rigidity lemma gives \[ A(T)=E(\F_2),\qquad A(E)=E(\F_2)\oplus\operatorname{End}_{\F_2}(E). \] The cohomology boundary therefore injects \(\operatorname{End}_{\F_2}(E)\) into \(H^1_{\et}(S,A)\). In particular \(\alpha=\delta(1_E)\) has infinite order: \([m]:E\to E\) has degree \(m^2\) and is nonconstant for every nonzero integer \(m\). To represent this class by a scheme, glue two copies \(X_i=E\times T\) along \(E\times E\), using the identity on one side and \((a,t)\mapsto(a+t,t)\) on the other. Both attaching maps are closed immersions, so the pushout is a scheme by the Stacks Project, Lemma~37.67.8; Lemma~37.67.9(4) gives smoothness over \(S\)~\cite{BStacksClosedPushout,BStacksPushoutMorphisms}. The same local lifting just used trivializes the translation cocycle on an etale cover. Thus this scheme is the \(A\)-torsor of class \(\pm\alpha\), locally isomorphic to \(E\times S\), and is proper with geometrically connected genus-one fibres. Under the principal polarization \(E\simeq E^\vee\), translation by \(a\) acts on \(\operatorname{Pic}^d(E)\) by translation by \(\pm da\): represent a divisor by its sum in \(E\). Consequently \(\operatorname{Pic}^d_{X/S}\) is a torsor of class \(\pm d\alpha\). A global line bundle of degree \(d\) would give a section of that torsor, forcing \(d\alpha=0\), hence \(d=0\). This proves the assertion, and also shows that \(X\to S\) is not projective. The cubic smoothness, its five \(\F_2\)-points, and the displayed fibre-product algebra were checked exactly by \texttt{part\_b/code/singular\_genus\_one\_checks.py}; its output is preserved with the computations. The infinite-order and torsor claims are proved above, not inferred from the finite computation.
status: Proved counterexample to an extension beyond the stated manuscript scope
notes: S is two P2 overF2 glued along the explicit smooth elliptic cubic. Translation by id_E glues a proper smooth genus-one torsor of infinite period. Pic^d has class d alpha, so every line bundle has degree0. This is not a Brauer-infinitude counterexample and lies outside the regular scope of12:79.

statement: A fully specified nonzero degree-two group on 12:78: Let \(C/\F_2\) be the good reduction of the displayed \(X_0(11)\) model, and let \(A=C\times C\to C\) be its constant Jacobian scheme. Take \(\ell=3\). Direct enumeration gives \(\#C(\F_2)=5\), so Frobenius on \(V_3C\) has polynomial \(t^2+2t+2\). Its two roots are distinct, and the centralizer of a companion matrix has dimension two. Kummer, the constant-case result just proved, and Hochschild--Serre give \[ V_3H^2_{\et}(C,A) \simeq H^2_{\Bcts}(C,V_3A) \simeq H^1_{\Bcts}(\bar C,V_3A)_\Gamma \simeq\End_{\F_2}(C)\otimes\Q_3, \] of dimension two. The geometric degree-two term has weight one, so contributes no invariants; in the degree-one term, \(H^1(\bar C,\Q_3)\otimes V_3C=(V_3C)^\vee\otimes V_3C\). Semisimplicity identifies its coinvariants with its invariants, and Tate's Main Theorem identifies the latter with endomorphisms. The point count and exact centralizer calculation are reproduced in \texttt{part\_b/code/finite\_field\_checks.py}. This verifies the intended nonvanishing in R6. If a dual Tate module is replaced in the transcription by the Tate module of the dual abelian variety, a twist must be retained: \((V_\ell J)^\vee=V_\ell(J^t)(-1)\). An integral isomorphism also cannot be read off from a displayed \(\Q_\ell\)-vector-space calculation without tracking finite Kummer kernels.
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: All rational twists on the compactified integer ring: In the Flach--Morin theory of \(\overline{\Spec\Z}\), \[ H^i_{\BW}(\overline{\Spec\Z},\Q(n))= \begin{cases} \Q,&(n,i)=(0,0)\text{ or }(1,3),\\ \Q,&n\ge3\text{ odd},\ i=1,\\ \Q,&n\le-2\text{ even},\ i=2,\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases}\tag{B.5} \] The unit in degree zero pairs perfectly with the fundamental class in degree three and twist one. For every odd \(n\ge3\), the degree-one regulator line in twist \(n\) pairs perfectly with the degree-two line in twist \(1-n\). The dualizing object is \(\Q(1)[3]\).
notes: Nonzero exactly (n,i)=(0,0),(1,3), positive odd n>=3 i1, negative even n<=-2 i2.

statement: The omitted order-two groups: The two integral tables asserted in 15:173 are false in Flach--Morin Weil--etale cohomology. Their correct values are \[ H^i_{\BW}(\overline{\Spec\Z},\Z(1))= \begin{cases}\Z/2,&i=1,\\\Z,&i=3,\\0,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases} \qquad H^i_{\BW}(\overline{\Spec\Z},\Z)= \begin{cases}\Z,&i=0,\\\Z/2,&i=3,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\tag{B.7} \]
notes: Missing Z/2 in twist1 degree1 and twist0 degree3.

statement: The complete structural table: For \(m\ge2\), put \(C_m=H^2_{\et}(\Spec\Z,\Z(m))\), a finite group, and \(a_m=1\) for odd \(m\ge3\), \(a_m=0\) for even \(m\). Let \(w_m\) be the order of \(H^0(\Q,\Q/\Z(m))\). Explicitly, \[ w_m=\begin{cases} 2,&m\text{ odd},\\ 2^{2+v_2(m)}\displaystyle\prod_{\substack{p\text{ odd prime}\\p-1\mid m}} p^{1+v_p(m)},&m\text{ even}. \end{cases} \] Define \(\epsilon_{i,n}\) to be one if \(i\equiv n\pmod2\) and either \(1\le i\le n\) or \(n<i<0\), and zero otherwise. In addition to (B.7), all the integral groups have the following structure: \[ H^i_{\BW}(\overline{\Spec\Z},\Z(n))\simeq \begin{cases} \Z^{a_n}\oplus\Z/w_n,&n>1,\ i=1,\\ C_n,&n>1,\ i=2,\\ (\Z/2)^{\epsilon_{i,n}},&n>1,\ i\ge3,\\ (\Z/2)^{\epsilon_{i-1,n}},&n<0,\ i<0,\\ \Z^{a_{1-n}}\oplus C_{1-n}^{D},&n<0,\ i=2,\\ \Z/w_{1-n},&n<0,\ i=3,\\ 0,&\text{all remaining cases with }n\notin\{0,1\}. \end{cases}\tag{B.22} \] The direct-sum splittings and generators of the free groups in this display are not canonical. The arithmetic computation denoted by \(C_m\) is explicitly supplied by the two following results.
notes: Rational table complete; every finite C_m now has a terminating arithmetic presentation including 2-primary generators; primitive integral free generators now have an audited terminating cycle-and-boundary search; no uniform Vandiver vanishing is claimed.; Explicit roots-of-unity torsion and real2 terms; finite C_m have explicit terminating arithmetic presentations.

statement: Every two-primary entry and its generator: For the finite group \(C_m\) in (B.22), \[ C_m[2^\infty]= \begin{cases}\Z/2,&m\ge2\text{ even},\\0,&m\ge3\text{ odd}. \end{cases} \] For even \(m\), a generator is the inverse image, under the canonical localization and completion isomorphism, of \[ \delta\bigl(\iota_m([-1])\bigr) \in H^2(\Spec\Z[1/2],\Z_2(m)). \] Here \([-1]\in H^1(\Spec\Z[1/2],\Z/2)\) is the Kummer class of \(-1\), \(\iota_m:\Z/2\to\Q_2/\Z_2(m)\) is the order-two inclusion, and \(\delta\) is the connecting map for \(0\to\Z_2(m)\to\Q_2(m)\to\Q_2/\Z_2(m)\to0\).
notes: Scoped statement status; consult the item ledger for the original task.

statement: Finite arithmetic computation of each odd-primary term: \status{Proved} Fix an integer \(n\ge2\). There is an unconditional terminating algorithm, specified below using integer polynomial enumeration and finite matrices, which returns the invariant factors and cohomological generators of the odd-primary subgroup of \(C_n=H^2_{\et}(\Spec\Z,\Z(n))\). It requires neither Vandiver's conjecture nor a class-group vanishing assertion. This is an effective presentation, not a claim that the resulting invariant factors obey one presently proved closed vanishing pattern.
status: Proved as a terminating effective presentation
notes: Root proof independently audited: explicit prime and field bounds, crossed-cocycle matrix, compact-support duality, successive-order stop criterion. Not a uniform Vandiver vanishing claim.

statement: An integral generator specified by finite searches: For each odd integer \(m\ge3\), the following procedure specifies an higher Chow cycle \(\gamma_m\) over \(\Q\) with integer coefficients whose canonical integral-base class generates \[ H^1_{\et}(\Spec\Z,\Z(m))/\mathrm{tors} \simeq\Z. \] Every search terminates. The procedure requires the finite arithmetic computation of \(C_m\) in Theorem~\ref{thm:B-effective-odd-torsion} and Proposition~\ref{prop:B-two-primary}, but requires no uniform vanishing conjecture for these groups. Its output is a cycle given by rational polynomial equations and integer multiplicities, together with an explicitly found boundary certifying the saturation step.
notes: Existence and regulator survive the explicit-formula source error. Search actual admissible corrections, clear their denominators, compute exact index from special values, then enumerate an integral primitive cycle with a bounding-chain certificate.

statement: The degeneracy in the displayed uniform correction: For every weight \(m\ge4\), the displayed \(W_2^{(i)}\) terms in Kerr--Yang \S4D are cubically degenerate, or zero, as rational higher Chow cycles. Their existence theorem used above does not depend on those displayed terms.
status: Proved source-formula defect; no general boundary formula asserted
notes: KerrLi confirms first K7 W2 is degenerate and cycle not closed. Every uniform Section4D W2 is homogeneous in u,v except final coordinate v minus1; substitution u=sv proves its degeneracy for all weights. No complete all-weight boundary formula is asserted or used.

statement: An exact Vandiver gate inside B.4: Fix an odd prime \(p\), set \(L=\Q(\zeta_p)\), \(\Delta=\Gal(L/\Q)\), and let \(A\) be the \(p\)-primary part of \(\BCl(\mathcal O_L)\). Write \(A[j]\) for its \(\omega^j\)-eigenspace, where \(\omega\) is the Teichmuller character. For every \(m\ge2\), \[ H^2_{\Bcts}(\Z[1/p],\Z_p(m))/p \simeq (A/p\otimes\mu_p^{\otimes(m-1)})^\Delta \simeq A[1-m]/p.\tag{B.23} \] Consequently the simultaneous assertion \[ C_m[p^\infty]=0\quad\text{for every odd }m\ge3 \] is equivalent to the \(p\)-instance of Vandiver's conjecture, \(p\nmid h(\Q(\zeta_p)^+)\).
notes: All odd m>=3 for each fixed odd p; current 2026 partial-regularity source does not prove universal assertion.

statement: A certified irregular-prime instance: Let \(L=\Q(\zeta_{37}+\zeta_{37}^{-1})\), with \(\zeta_{37}\) a primitive thirty-seventh root of unity. The preserved PARI/GP computation constructs its degree-eighteen real cyclotomic polynomial, returns the trivial computed class group, and returns \(1\) from \texttt{bnfcertify(B,1)}. The documented meaning of that flag is that the actual class group is a quotient of the computed group; since the latter is trivial, the actual class group is trivial \cite{BPariClass2026}. Consequently \(C_m[37^\infty]=0\) for every odd \(m\ge3\), by Proposition~\ref{prop:B-Vandiver}. The same exact computation gives \[ \frac{B_{32}}{32}=-\frac{7709321041217}{16320},\qquad v_{37}(B_{32}/32)=1, \] so this is an irregular prime instance. The executable input is \path{part_b/code/vandiver37_quotient.gp}; the full polynomial, certificate output, PARI version \(2.19.1\), and elapsed time \(47\) milliseconds are in \path{part_b/output/vandiver37_quotient.txt}. The interrupted stronger full-unit certification is retained as unused output and plays no role in this proof.
status: Proved by a complete arithmetic certificate
notes: Class group of maximal real cyclotomic subfield is a quotient of computed trivial group; v37(B32/32)=1 confirms irregularity. All positive odd-twist C_m have zero37-primary part.

statement: Finite absolute duality, with the coefficient category specified: Let \(X\) be regular, separated, and of finite type over \(\Spec\Z\), of pure absolute dimension \(d\). Let \(F\) be a bounded constructible complex of \(\Z/m\)-sheaves on \(X_{\et}\). There is a perfect pairing of finite groups \[ \widehat H_c^i(X,F)\ \times\ \operatorname{Ext}^{2d+1-i}_{X,\Z/m} (F,\Z/m(d))\longrightarrow\Q/\Z.\tag{B.26} \] Here \(\Z/m(d)\) is the etale motivic complex, the Ext is in the derived category of \(\Z/m\)-sheaves, and the hat denotes the Tate modification at real places. If \(m\) is invertible on \(X\), \(\Z/m(d)\simeq\mu_m^{\otimes d}\). Thus, for a locally constant finite free \(F\), the second factor is the cohomology of the usual twisted dual sheaf. The real-place modification disappears for odd \(m\), for schemes with no real fibre, and for schemes over a finite field; properness over \(\Spec\Z\) alone does not remove it.
notes: Use etale motivic Z/m(d) if m noninvertible and Tate-modified real compact support.

statement: Finite duality without separatedness: The finite pairing (B.26) extends to every regular finite-type \(\Z\)-scheme of pure dimension \(d\), when compact support on a possibly nonseparated scheme is defined by the following finite open-cover construction. This definition agrees with the usual Tate-modified compact support when the scheme is separated.
status: Proved for compact support defined by open-cover descent
notes: Functorial finite alternating compact-support Cech chain totalization is cover-independent by refinement. The exact j! simplex resolution computes the dual Ext totalization. Real modifications glue termwise; no nonseparated compactification is assumed.

statement: Rational duality for the Tate cases proved here: For \(X=\Spec\mathcal O_K\), the Flach--Morin compactified complexes have perfect rational pairings \[ H^i_{\BW}(\bar X,\Q(n))\times H^{3-i}_{\BW}(\bar X,\Q(1-n))\longrightarrow\Q. \tag{B.27} \] For \(U=\Spec\mathcal O_K[1/S]\), the same assertion pairs the localized rational absolute complex with the compact-support complex, with the archimedean completion inherited from \(\bar X\). For a smooth projective geometrically connected curve \(C/\F_q\), the corresponding Weil--etale pairing is \[ H^i_{\BW}(C,\Q(n))\times H^{3-i}_{\BW}(C,\Q(1-n)) \longrightarrow\Q. \tag{B.28} \] Both statements hold for every integral twist \(n\), including negative twists, and for finite direct sums of these Tate objects.
notes: Open number-ring complex specified by localization and compact support; arbitrary M remains separate.

statement: Finite-monodromy coefficient motives: Let \(X\) be either an open number ring or a smooth projective curve over a finite field. Let \(W\) be a finite-dimensional rational representation of a finite quotient of \(\pi_1^{\et}(X)\). Then the rational absolute or Weil--etale theory just specified has a common rational structure for all \(W(n)\), every integer \(n\), and perfect pairings \[ H^i_{\rm abs}(X,W(n))\ \times\ H^{3-i}_{\rm abs,c}(X,W^\vee(1-n))\longrightarrow\Q. \] Compact support includes the stated archimedean completion on a number ring; it is unnecessary for a proper finite-field curve. The degree-one realization is the Bloch--Kato finite-condition group with the same geometric conditions at the omitted places.
notes: Finite cover, invariant projector, restriction/corestriction for local conditions, and averaged perfect evaluation give all twists on number rings and proper finite-field curves.

statement: The exact number-ring rational gate for a dual pair: Fix a pure coefficient motive \(M/K\), and write \(M^*=M^\vee(1)\). Suppose rational motivic spaces \(A^a(M)\) and \(A^a(M^*)\), for \(a=0,1\), are specified with their realization maps. They admit a finite-dimensional rational dual completion having the graded Selmer comparisons in every degree if and only if the degree-zero and degree-one maps for both motives satisfy Fontaine's f-admissibility conditions \(c^0_\ell,c^1_\ell\) for every \(\ell\). For the prescribed motivic spaces, this is a genuine realization conjecture, not the assertion that some abstract vector spaces of the same dimensions can be chosen.
status: Proved equivalence for dual completions; the realization hypothesis is conjectural
notes: Direct-sum dual completion is sufficient and necessity is its degree0/1 comparison. No six-operation motivic category or canonical higher comparison is silently asserted.

statement: Pointed partitions: Let $\mathcal P_k$ be the set of partitions of $\{0,1,\ldots,k\}$. The block containing $0$ is the distinguished block. For $P\in\mathcal P_k$, put $J=P(0)\setminus\{0\}$ and define \[ \varepsilon_P=\prod_{i\in J}y_i\prod_{B\in P,\,0\notin B}\delta_B, \qquad d(P)=k-|P|+1. \] Here $\delta_B$ is the pullback of the small diagonal in $X^B$ and $\delta_{\{i\}}=1$. Thus $\varepsilon_P\in T_k[d(P)]$. This describes the pointed and unpointed partial diagonals of manuscript 11:55 without duplicate notation.
notes: Definition used throughout C.1.

statement: C.1(b): the complete graph product rule: Choose a tree on each block of $P$ and of $Q$, using the edges $\{0,i\}$ in a distinguished block, and take the union as a multigraph on $\{0,\ldots,k\}$. Write $b(C)=|E(C)|-|V(C)|+1$ for the cycle rank of a connected component. A component not containing $0$ contributes \[ \begin{cases} \delta_C,&b(C)=0,\\ \chi(X)\prod_{i\in C}y_i,&b(C)=1,\\ 0,&b(C)\geq2, \end{cases} \] whereas the component containing $0$ contributes $\prod_{i\in C\setminus\{0\}}y_i$ if $b(C)=0$, and zero otherwise. Multiplying these contributions gives $\varepsilon_P\varepsilon_Q$, independently of the chosen trees. In particular, the $\varepsilon_P$ span $T_k$.
notes: Checked for 2286 graph pairs in finite models.

statement: C.1(a): all relations from the multilinear forms: Choose a homogeneous basis $(e_a)$ of $A$, containing $e_0=1$. For fixed $d$, form a matrix $C_{k,d}$ whose columns are the partitions $P$ with $d(P)=d$ and whose rows are the basis tensors $e_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{a_k}$ of total degree $D(k-d)$. Its entry is \begin{equation} (C_{k,d})_{\mathbf a,P} =\epsilon(\mathbf a,P) \prod_{B\in P,\,0\notin B}\kappa\Bigl(\prod_{i\in B}e_{a_i}\Bigr) \prod_{i\in P(0)\setminus\{0\}}[a_i=0]. \end{equation} In each block the indices are in increasing order; $\epsilon$ is the Koszul sign of collecting the factors into those blocks. Then \[ \dim_L T_k[d]=\operatorname{rank}_L C_{k,d},\qquad \sum_Pc_P\varepsilon_P=0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ (c_P)_P\in\ker C_{k,d}. \] A finite presentation of $T_k$ consists of one variable $z_P$ for each $P\in\mathcal P_k$, the unit relation, all product relations of Theorem~\ref{c:graph-rule}, and one linear relation for each vector in a basis of each $\ker C_{k,d}$. Thus Gaussian elimination gives generators for the entire ideal of relations. The input is exactly the graded vector space, its unit and trace, and the multilinear forms $\kappa(u_1\cdots u_m)$ on positive-degree elements.
notes: Gaussian elimination gives all linear relations; uses full ambient pairing.

statement: The modified diagonal and the correction to R8: The class \[ M=\delta_{123}-\delta_{12}y_3-\delta_{23}y_1-\delta_{13}y_2 +y_1y_2+y_2y_3+y_1y_3 \in H^{4n}(X^3) \] vanishes if and only if $\kappa(uvw)=0$ for every three positive-degree classes $u,v,w$. The degree $H^{2n}$ stated in R8 is incorrect when $n$ denotes the geometric dimension. Neither $M$ nor its higher-arity analogues, without further dimension relations, generate all relations in every $T_k$.
status: Proved; proposed generation by this relation alone refuted
notes: P1 with k=2 refutes M-only generation; correct cohomology degree is 4n.

statement: Dimensions for curves and for surfaces with $b_1=0$: For a curve of genus $g$, put $b=-2g$; for a smooth projective surface with $b_1=0$, put $b=b_2$. Define $q_{ij}=\delta_{ij}-y_i-y_j$. All relations are generated by \begin{align} y_i^2&=0,&y_iq_{ij}&=0,&q_{ij}^2&=b\,y_iy_j,&q_{ij}q_{ik}&=y_iq_{jk}, \end{align} and the following dimension relations, with all displayed indices distinct. For a surface they are \begin{equation} \sum_{\sigma\in S_{b+1}}\sgn(\sigma) \prod_{a=1}^{b+1}q_{i_a,j_{\sigma(a)}}=0; \end{equation} for a curve they are \begin{equation} \sum_{\text{perfect matchings }\mathcal M\text{ on }2g+2\text{ slots}} \prod_{\{i,j\}\in\mathcal M}q_{ij}=0. \end{equation} There is no sign in \eqref{c:sympl-pf}, because the symplectic signs are already included by the odd degree of $H^1$ and the Koszul constraint. For a partition $\lambda$, write $f^\lambda$ for the number of standard Young tableaux of shape $\lambda$, explicitly $|\lambda|!$ divided by the product of the hook lengths. Put \[ r_b(m)= \begin{cases} \displaystyle\sum_{\lambda\vdash m,\,\ell(\lambda)\leq b} f^{2\lambda},&b\geq0\quad\text{(surface)},\\[4pt] \displaystyle\sum_{\lambda\vdash m,\,\lambda_1\leq g} f^{2\lambda},&b=-2g\quad\text{(curve)}, \end{cases} \qquad r_b(0)=1. \] Then the answer in every degree is \begin{equation} \dim T_k[d]= \sum_{\substack{m\geq0,\ a=d-m\geq0\\a+2m\leq k}} \frac{k!}{a!(2m)!(k-a-2m)!}\,r_b(m). \end{equation} The curve formula includes $g=0$, when $r_0(m)=0$ for $m>0$ and the answer is $\binom{k}{d}$.
notes: Finite numerical ranks checked against hook-length formulas.

statement: Explicit dimension algorithms for projective spaces and abelian varieties: The following finite integer matrices determine every dimension by ordinary exact rational rank; in particular they give a uniform computable answer for every $n,g,k,d$, with no geometric unknown in their entries. For $X=\mathbb P^n$, the columns are $P\in\mathcal P_k$ with $d(P)=d$, and the rows are $(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\in\{0,\ldots,n\}^k$ with $\sum a_i=nd$. The entry is $1$ precisely when \[ a_i=n\quad(i\in P(0)\setminus\{0\}),\qquad \sum_{i\in B}a_i=n(|B|-1)\quad(0\notin B), \] and is zero otherwise. Its rank is $\dim T_k[d]$. For an abelian variety of dimension $g>0$, use the exterior algebra on the $2gk$ symbols $e_{i,a}$, ordered lexicographically. In this algebra put \[ y_i=\prod_{a=1}^{2g}e_{i,a},\qquad \delta_{ij}=\prod_{a=1}^{2g}(e_{i,a}-e_{j,a}). \] For each $P$ multiply these expressions along any of its trees and its pinned vertices. The coefficient matrix in the exterior-monomial basis of degree $2gd$ has entries in $\Z$ and rank $\dim T_k[d]$. These ranks depend only on $g,k,d$.
notes: Explicit rank algorithms in every k and degree; no unsupported closed simplification.

statement: The abelian and hyperelliptic cases: For an abelian variety with $o$ its origin, every cohomological relation in the rings of C.1(a) holds in $T_k^{\CH}(X,o)$ for every $k$. The same conclusion holds for a hyperelliptic curve with $o$ a Weierstrass point (and for an elliptic curve with its origin and for $\mathbb P^1$).
status: Known, with the required implication proved
notes: The K3 all-powers assertion is not included here.

statement: Classification of the allowed zero-cycles on an abelian variety: Let $A/F$ be an abelian variety over an algebraically closed field of any characteristic, and let $o\in\CH_0(A)_\Q$ have degree one. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item all the cohomological point-and-diagonal relations hold in $T_k^{\CH}(A,o)$ for every $k$; \item $\Delta_*o=o\boxtimes o$ in $\CH_0(A\times A)_\Q$; \item $o=[a]$ in $\CH_0(A)_\Q$ for a point $a\in A(F)$. \end{enumerate} The point is unique modulo torsion in $A(F)$. In particular, specifying the origin is sufficient but is not necessary for the requested lifting.
status: Proved over every algebraically closed field
notes: Includes positive characteristic and2; necessity already the T2 group-like relation.

statement: A finite criterion for curves: Let $C$ be a smooth projective connected curve and $o\in\CH_0(C)_\Q$ have degree one. All point-and-diagonal cohomological relations hold in all its powers if and only if $M_o=0$ in $\CH^2(C^3)_\Q$. If $g\geq2$, this forces \[ o=\frac{K_C}{2g-2}\quad\text{in }\CH^1(C)_\Q. \] For $g=0$ or $1$ every degree-one rational zero-cycle has the required property. Over $\C$, the genus-at-least-two criterion is also the multiplicativity criterion in \citet[Propositions 3.1 and 3.5]{c_fulaterveervial2021}.
status: Proved over every algebraically closed field
notes: For g>=2 uniquely o=K/(2g-2); for g0,1 every rational degree-one class works.

statement: The exact additional obstruction for regular surfaces: Let $S/\C$ be a smooth projective surface with $b_1(S)=0$, and let $o$ have degree one. All the point-and-diagonal cohomological relations lift in all powers if and only if $M_o=0$ and $h(S)$ is Kimura finite-dimensional. If they hold, $o$ is uniquely determined: for every ample divisor $H$, \[ o=\frac{H^2}{\deg H^2}. \]
status: Proved equivalence; does not assume finite-dimensionality
notes: Does not assert finite-dimensionality; o necessarily H^2/deg(H^2).

statement: A finite cycle criterion when the cohomology is even: Let $X/\C$ be smooth projective and connected, with $H^{\rm odd}(X,\Q)=0$, let $n=\dim X>0$, and let $o\in\CH^n(X)_\Q$ have degree $1$. Put $d=\dim_\Q H^*(X,\Q)=\chi(X)$. There is a finite list of rational tensor expressions $P_1,\ldots,P_s$, constructed by the procedure below from the rational cup-product table and trace of $X$, for which the following criterion is necessary and sufficient for all the relations of Theorem~\ref{c:matrix-presentation} to hold in rational Chow groups on every power: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $c_n(T_X)=d\,o$ and $\Delta_*o=o\boxtimes o$; \item $\bigwedge^{d+1}h(X)=0$ in rational Chow motives; \item $P_a(h(X),\mu,1,\operatorname{tr},o,\beta^{-1})=0$ for $1\leq a\leq s$. \end{enumerate} Here $\mu$ is the small-diagonal multiplication, $\operatorname{tr}:h(X)\to\Q(-n)$ is the trace, $\beta=\operatorname{tr}\circ\mu$, and $\beta^{-1}:\Q(-n)\to h(X)\otimes h(X)$ is its inverse pairing. Every condition is the vanishing of a specified finite linear combination of correspondence diagrams. Subject to (i), each can equivalently be written as a finite list of cycles in the requested point-and-diagonal rings. The construction uses finite-dimensional polynomial algebra, so is a finite criterion, rather than one separate test for each power of $X$.
notes: Finite covariant relations plus exterior vanishing and two normalization identities; does not decide their rational equivalence algorithmically.

statement: Scope of the finite criterion: Theorem~\ref{c:finite-even-criterion} applies to arbitrary cup-product algebras with pure-even cohomology, not only to surfaces. It gives a finite algebraic construction of the cycle conditions, without claiming to decide their rational equivalence by computation. For general mixed cohomology the analogous direct use of $\operatorname{GL}_{a|b}$ would require exactness of its invariant functor, which fails. A chosen Chow parity splitting would permit the ordinary reductive group $\operatorname{GL}_a\times \operatorname{GL}_b$ and the even and odd dimension relations, but its existence is an additional issue and it need not lie in the requested tautological correspondence category. The unrestricted classification of all $(X,o)$ therefore remains distinct from the specific K3 obstruction proved below.
status: Proved scope clarification; the arbitrary-pair classification remains unresolved
notes: D supplies an explicit odd-derivation certificate for the marked cohomology of E times P1.

statement: The narrow K3 ring already detects finite-dimensionality: Let $S/\C$ be a projective K3 surface and let $o$ be its Beauville--Voisin class. The following assertions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item for every $k$, all the cohomological relations among the point and diagonal classes hold in $\CH^*(S^k)_\Q$; \item with $\pi_2=\Delta_S-o\times S-S\times o$, the cycle \begin{equation} D_{23}=\sum_{\sigma\in S_{23}}\sgn(\sigma) \prod_{a=1}^{23}(\pi_2)_{a,23+\sigma(a)} \quad\text{vanishes in }\CH^{46}(S^{46})_\Q; \end{equation} \item $\bigwedge^{23}h^2(S)=0$ in rational Chow motives; \item $h(S)$ is finite-dimensional in the sense of Kimura--O'Sullivan. \end{enumerate} Thus the request for every K3 surface is not supplied by the Beauville--Voisin small-diagonal theorem. The first missing universal determinant for this narrower ring occurs on $46$ factors.
status: Proved equivalence; the general vanishing is unresolved
notes: First missing narrow determinant is on46 factors; equivalent transcendental test is on2(23-rho) factors, using divisor projectors; general vanishing not proved.

statement: Removing the algebraic part of the K3 gate: Let $S/\C$ be a projective K3 surface of Picard rank $\rho$, let $D_1,\ldots,D_\rho$ be a rational basis of $\operatorname{NS}(S)_\Q$, and let $B=(\deg D_aD_b)_{a,b}$. Define \[ \pi_{\rm alg}=\sum_{a,b}(B^{-1})_{ab}D_a\times D_b, \qquad \pi_{\rm tr}=\pi_2-\pi_{\rm alg},\qquad t_2(S)=(S,\pi_{\rm tr},0). \] Every assertion of Theorem~\ref{c:k3-gate} is also equivalent to \[ \bigwedge^{23-\rho}t_2(S)=0. \] Equivalently, the alternating sum of the products $(\pi_{\rm tr})_{a,,23-\rho+\sigma(a)}$, over $\sigma\in S_{23-\rho}$, vanishes on $S^{,2(23-\rho)}$. For Picard rank $1$ this is a test on $44$ factors. This smaller correspondence uses divisor classes outside the narrow requested ring; its factor count therefore does not contradict the unconditional narrow-ring result through $45$ factors.
status: Proved smaller equivalent vanishing test; general vanishing unresolved
notes: Picard rank1 gives44 factors with divisor projectors outside the narrow ring; narrow first determinant remains on46 factors.

statement: The unconditional K3 range: For every projective complex K3 surface with its Beauville--Voisin class, the requested relations hold in every power $S^k$ with $k\leq45$. More generally they hold in normalized degree $d$ of every $S^k$ whenever \[ \min(d,k-d)\leq22, \] where normalized degree $d$ means Chow codimension $2d$. In this range no finite-dimensionality assumption is required.
notes: First unproved universal determinant occurs at k46,d23; codimension is2d.

statement: An explicit genus-three failure: Let $C/\C$ be the plane quartic $X^4+Y^4=Z^4$, and take $o=(0:1:1)$. Its modified diagonal $M_o$ vanishes in every Weil cohomology, but \[ M_o\ne0\quad\hbox{in }\CH^2(C^3)_\Q. \] Thus the cohomological relation in Proposition~\ref{c:modified-diagonal} fails in rational Chow groups for this completely specified genus-three pointed curve.
notes: Smooth genus three; Bloch proves Sigma non-torsion modulo algebraic equivalence; exact odd sum-map pushforward is 3 Sigma in Chow.

statement: A gauged special bivariant system: Over a characteristic-zero field $L$, a special bivariant system assigns to every finite set $I$ a finite-dimensional graded-commutative algebra $A(I)$, with $A(\varnothing)=L$, a trace $\kappa_I$ of degree $-D|I|$, and a perfect trace pairing. For a map $\alpha:I\to J$ it assigns \[ \alpha^*:A(I)\longrightarrow A(J),\qquad \alpha_*:A(J)\longrightarrow A(I). \] The first is a unital graded algebra homomorphism; the second has degree $D(|I|-|J|)$. Pullbacks compose covariantly in maps of indexing sets, pushforwards contravariantly, and \[ \kappa_I(\alpha_*x\,a)=\kappa_J(x\,\alpha^*a),\qquad \alpha_*(x\alpha^*a)=\alpha_*x\,a. \] For disjoint unions the exterior-product maps $A(I)\otimes A(J)\to A(I\amalg J)$ are isomorphisms compatible with associativity, units, traces, and the Koszul symmetry. These maps are compatible with pullback and pushforward. The exchange axiom is base change for product squares (a projection pulled back by a map on the other factor); arbitrary self-intersection squares are not included. The gauge is the chosen trace, not a quotient up to multiplication by a scalar. A morphism in the bivariant category from $A$ to $B$ is a pair $(f^*,f_*)$, with $f^*:B\to A$ a unital graded algebra map and $f_*:A\to B$ its trace adjoint. On powers these maps are tensor powers and satisfy the corresponding pullback and pushforward compatibilities. The adjoint need not preserve the unit.
status: Definition, with the corrected exchange axiom
notes: Unrestricted Cartesian base change excluded explicitly.

statement: C.2: equivalence and the exchange axiom: Special gauged bivariant systems are equivalent to finite-dimensional graded-commutative Frobenius algebras of even top degree, with bivariant adjoint morphisms. The functor taking a system to its one-factor algebra and diagonal coevaluation is fully faithful. For a smooth projective connected variety, $I\mapsto H^*(X^I)$ satisfies these axioms. Correspondence composition defined by these axioms is associative and has the diagonal as identity.
status: Proved, with the category specified above
notes: Includes full faithfulness, Weil cohomology example, and associativity.

statement: The R7 hypotheses used in this Part: We checked the proof in the supplied reading, \S\S2.1--2.3, against 12:150--158. The conditional construction there is not a construction of a faithful realization on all Chow motives: it first quotients by the chosen homological equivalence, assumes its equality with numerical equivalence and the stated positivity, and then takes the semisimple envelope. Our Chow assertions above do not use this conditional passage. In particular it cannot be used to kill the homologically zero K3 determinant. The sign correction is forced by the cross-product formula: interchanging a class of degree $a$ with one of degree $b$ multiplies it by $(-1)^{ab}$. Thus the original realization is symmetric into graded vector spaces with that commutativity constraint. This is the convention used in our Frobenius equivalence. A level filtration by thick subcategories yields a direct-sum level decomposition only when the ambient category is semisimple; then we group the simple constituents according to their least allowed twist. Thickness alone gives no splitting of extensions. The geometric level definition of C.4 therefore does not assert a canonical splitting or identify itself with coniveau. The internal-Hom error of 12:156 already occurs in the semisimple effective Tate category with objects finite sums of $\Q(-a)$, $a\geq0$. For every effective $Z$, \[ \Hom(Z\otimes\Q(-1),\Q)=0. \] Hence the effective internal Hom from $\Q(-1)$ to $\Q$ is the zero object. After adjoining all Tate twists the corresponding internal Hom is $\Q(1)$, which is nonzero. Thus effective internal Homs need not be preserved by Tate inversion. In a rigid tensor category the valid identity is \[ \underline{\Hom}(M,N(-i)) =M^\vee\otimes N(-i) =M^*\otimes N, \qquad M^*=M^\vee(-i). \] Evaluation and coevaluation give these isomorphisms and their inverse maps. Merely postulating the effective object $M^*$ without the duality identities does not prove them. These checks confirm precisely the restrictions of R7 needed here.
status: Used and rechecked, with its internal-Hom counterexample confirmed
notes: No homological realization faithfulness on Chow motives inferred from the conditional construction.

statement: The invariant-centre identity: For a pro-reductive group $G$ over a characteristic-zero field, \[ \Hom_G(\mathbf1,\Lie G)=(\Lie G)^G=\Lie Z(G). \] If $G$ is connected, the map from its centre to its abelianization induces an isomorphism on Lie algebras. If $G^\circ$ has protorus abelianization $S$ and $\Gamma=G/G^\circ$, then \[ (\Lie G)^G=(\Lie S)^\Gamma. \] The invariant condition under $\Gamma$ cannot be discarded.
notes: Pro-reductive inverse-limit version included.

statement: Lead C3 with its arithmetic action: Let $K$ be finitely generated over $\Q$, embedded in $\C$, and let $K_0$ be the algebraic closure of $\Q$ in $K$. Suppose that the geometric connected motivic group is pro-reductive, that its maximal protorus quotient is the full Serre protorus $S$, and that the action of $\Gal(\overline K/K)$ on this quotient is the usual action through $\Gal(\overline\Q/K_0)$. If $E$ is the largest CM subfield of $K_0$, then \[ \dim_\Q (\Lie G)^G= \begin{cases}1+[E:\Q]/2,&E\text{ exists},\\1,&K_0\text{ has no CM subfield}. \end{cases} \] These hypotheses hold for the full category of motivated motives of abelian type, including Artin motives. The conclusion concerns the full arithmetic adjoint invariants; the centre of the geometric connected group alone is generally an infinite-dimensional pro-vector space.
status: Proved under the stated Serre-quotient hypothesis
notes: Geometric centre alone is generally infinite-dimensional.

statement: The finite-field analytic/algebraic distinction: Let $E/\F_5$ have equation $y^2=x^3-x$. It is smooth since its discriminant $64$ is nonzero modulo $5$. It has eight rational points, so geometric Frobenius has polynomial $T^2+2T+5$ on $H^1$ and eigenvalues $\pi=-1+2i$, $\bar\pi=-1-2i$. Its algebraic Frobenius torus is \[ T=\operatorname{Res}_{\Q(i)/\Q}\Gm, \qquad\dim T=2. \] Indeed the two primes of $\Q(i)$ above $5$ give valuations $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ on $(\pi,\bar\pi)$; hence $\pi^a\bar\pi^b=1$ implies $a=b=0$. There is consequently no character cutting out a proper algebraic subgroup containing Frobenius. The adjoint action of $T$ is trivial, so its whole Lie algebra is algebraic, but it is two-dimensional. On the other hand, for $\ell=3$ a suitable positive power of $\pi$ belongs to $1+3\Z_3[i]$. The analytic closure of the cyclic Frobenius subgroup has Lie algebra $\Q_3\log(\pi^N)$, of dimension one. The logarithm is nonzero because $\pi$ is not a root of unity. This is the distinction made by Serre in his letter of 8 September 1964, printed p.~202 of \citet{c_grothendieckserre}. Thus ``tout'' on 12:59 is valid for the adjoint Lie algebra of a commutative algebraic motivic band, as in the finite-field category under the Tate hypotheses of Part A; the accompanying identification with a single $\Q(0)$ does not describe that algebraic Lie object. Treating an analytic one-dimensional image as the motivic Lie algebra is an error, not an unconditional proof of a finite-field motivic assertion.
status: Proved counterexample to the one-dimensional algebraic reading
notes: Tout valid for commutative band; single Q(0) invalid for algebraic Lie interpretation.

statement: The level convention of 12:111--115: We fix $\ell$ invertible on the base and use $\Q_\ell(1)$ of weight $-2$. In the dimension-normalized convention, a special lisse sheaf of weight $r\geq0$ is a lisse subquotient of $R^rg_*\Q_\ell$ for a smooth projective morphism $g$ of relative dimension $r$. This includes the inserted dimension clause on 12:111; the transcription marks its following qualifier as uncertain. ``Strictly special'' means a direct summand, as clarified in 12:113. We explicitly call the version without a restriction on the relative dimension the broader convention. Over a field the two conventions agree, by the cut-and-pairing argument in Lemma~\ref{c:proper-level}; Theorem~\ref{c:general-level-bound} first uses the dimension-normalized convention, and Proposition~\ref{c:broader-coefficients} removes that clause for the general polygon and for the requested margin bound. Effective admissibility means that, after a finite stratification and the finite extensions allowed in 12:111, there is a finite filtration by extensions by zero of such sheaves. A sheaf has levels at most $\nu$ if these pieces may be chosen as $V(-a)$ with $a\geq0$, where $V$ is special of weight $r\leq\nu$. The simultaneous condition of weights in $\Phi$ requires the same pieces to satisfy $r+2a\in\Phi$. This is the geometric generation definition in 12:112; it is not simply a definition in terms of the eigenvalue weights, and it is not automatically the coniveau filtration.
notes: Not identified with a numerical weight bound or coniveau.

statement: C.4: the general $n-1$ bound is false: In the generality requested in the prompt, the bound \[ \operatorname{level}(R^if_*F)_{\bar y} \leq\min\{i,d_y(f)-1\}+j \] is false. Take $f:E\to\Spec\F_5$ for the elliptic curve in Example~\ref{c:finite-field-lie}, $F=\Q_\ell$, $j=0$, $i=1$, and any $\ell\ne5$. Then $d_y(f)=1$ and the right side is zero, whereas $H^1(E_{\overline\F_5},\Q_\ell)$ has level exactly one.
status: Refuted, with the precise manuscript correction
notes: Manuscript box is min(i,n)+j; margin has extra relative-dimension condition.

statement: Sharp elementary cases: If $f:X\to\Spec k$ is smooth projective of dimension $n$ and $F=\Q_\ell$, then $H^i(X)$ is pure of weight $i$ over a finite field and has level at most $\min(i,2n-i)$. Over a smooth pair $(Y,D)$ with a strict normal-crossing divisor and open immersion $j:Y\setminus D\hookrightarrow Y$, if $r$ branches meet at a geometric point $\bar y$, then \[ (R^ij_*\Q_\ell)_{\bar y}\simeq \bigwedge^i\bigl(\Q_\ell(-1)^r\bigr). \] It vanishes for $i>r$ and, when nonzero, has weight $2i$ and level zero. If a strictly special lisse sheaf extends across this pair, the projection formula tensors this description with its stalk.
notes: Universal replacement and margin now proved in c:general-level-bound under its explicit scope.

statement: The local dimension on 12:120: For a finite-type morphism $f:X\to Y$ of universally catenary noetherian schemes we use \[ d_y(f)=\sup_{\substack{x\in X\\ f(x)\text{ generalizes }y}} \left\{\operatorname{trdeg}_{k(f(x))}k(x) +\dim\overline{\{f(x)\}}^{\,\Spec\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\right\}. \] The closure in the second summand is taken in the local base. This is the dimension function, normalized to be zero at $y$, pulled back to $X$. It is the formula visible in the supplied transcription, whose notation for the local spectrum is uncertain. It measures local source dimension, not maximum fibre dimension: for $\Spec K\hookrightarrow\Spec R$ with $R$ a discrete valuation ring and $y$ its closed point it equals $1$, although all nonempty fibres have dimension zero. After an equidimensional localization of the source and a compactification, its maximum is the local dimension of that compactification. Regular alterations preserve this maximum. The dimension-function convention and the corresponding local cohomological interpretation are made precise in \citet[\S1.1.1 and Corollary 1.2.2]{c_pillonistroh2014}.
status: Definition, with the punctured-trait correction verified
notes: Not the Krull dimension of a nonproper localized source.

statement: Proper cohomology with simultaneous geometric bounds: Let $Z$ be proper of dimension at most $d$ over a field $k$, and let $a\geq0$. After the finite field extensions allowed in the admissibility definition, $H^a(Z_{\bar k},\Q_\ell)$ has a finite filtration by subquotients of special objects $V_r(-t)$ satisfying \[ t\geq\max(0,a-d),\qquad r\geq0,\qquad r+2t\leq a. \] In particular its weights are at most $a$ and its geometric levels are at most $\min(a,2d-a)$. A negative upper level bound means the object is zero. These are geometric generation assertions, not deductions from a Hodge polygon.
notes: Galois-quotient alteration and dimension induction preserve simultaneous bounds.

statement: Corrected bounds and the margin question: Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type, with $X$ regular and $X,Y$ of finite type over $\Z[1/\ell]$ or over a field of characteristic different from $\ell$. Fix $y\in Y$ and put $n=d_y(f)$. Let $F$ be strictly special of weight $j$, in the dimension-normalized sense of the insertion on 12:111: it is a direct summand of $R^jg_*\Q_\ell$ for a smooth projective $g$ of relative dimension $j$. Set $\epsilon=1$ if no component of local dimension $n$ maps to $y$, and set $\epsilon=0$ otherwise. Put \[ L=\max(0,i-n+\epsilon),\qquad U=\min(i,n)+j. \] The stalk $(R^if_*F)_{\bar y}$ is effectively admissible, with a filtration into pieces of weights $w$ and levels bounded simultaneously by \begin{equation} 2L\leq w\leq2U, \qquad \operatorname{level}\leq\min\{w-2L,\,2U-w\}. \end{equation} Consequently \[ \operatorname{weight}\leq2\min(i,n)+2j, \qquad \operatorname{level}\leq \begin{cases} \min(i,2n-i)+j,&\epsilon=0,\\ \min(i,2n-1-i)+j,&\epsilon=1. \end{cases} \] For an open immersion at a boundary point, $\epsilon=1$. The condition that $f$ have relative dimension at most $n-1$ near $y$ also implies $\epsilon=1$. Hence the margin's replacement by $n-1$ is valid with its stated extra condition, since $\min(i,2n-1-i)\leq\min(i,n-1)$. Without that condition the corrected general bound is at most $\min(i,n)+j$, and Proposition~\ref{c:level-counterexample} prevents replacing $n$ by $n-1$ universally.
status: Proved in the stated arithmetic finite-type setting
notes: Level min(i,2n-i)+j; margin/open-boundary level min(i,2n-1-i)+j; weight <=2min(i,n)+2j.

statement: Removing the dimension clause from the coefficient: Keep the finite-type hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{c:general-level-bound}, but suppose only that $F$ is a direct summand of $R^jg_*\Q_\ell$ for a smooth projective $g:Z\to X$ of arbitrary relative dimension. Put $n=d_y(f)$ and $L_0=\max(0,i-n)$, $U=\min(i,n)+j$. Then the simultaneous bounds \[ 2L_0\leq w\leq2U,\qquad \operatorname{level}\leq\min(w-2L_0,2U-w) \] still hold. In particular the general level bound is $\min(i,2n-i)+j$. If no component of local dimension $n$ maps to $y$, there is also the bound \[ \operatorname{level}\leq\min(i,n-1)+j. \] Consequently the requested weight bound and the manuscript's margin bound hold in this broader convention as well. The stronger margin polygon with $L_0$ replaced by $\max(0,i-n+1)$ remains covered by Theorem~\ref{c:general-level-bound} in its dimension-normalized convention.
notes: General level min(i,2n-i)+j and margin level min(i,n-1)+j. Stronger reflected margin polygon retains the normalized presentation in this proof.

statement: Optimality and the limit of the word sharp: For constant coefficients the preceding upper weight and level bounds are attained for every nonnegative degree in the indicated nonzero ranges. The general and margin level bounds remain optimal after adding $j$. The coefficient $2j$ in the universal weight envelope cannot be replaced by $j$: for every $j\geq0$ there is a strictly special weight-$j$ example with $n=i=1$ whose $R^1$ boundary stalk is pure of weight $2j+2$.
status: Proved optimality in the stated senses
notes: For j>0 weight envelope is attained in interior degrees. Top endpoint improved to2n+j; lower endpoint has exact local-invariant-cycle gate.

statement: The top degree and its sharper weight: In the finite-type setting of Theorem~\ref{c:general-level-bound}, let $F$ be any lisse $\Q_\ell$-sheaf. Then $(R^if_*F)_{\bar y}=0$ for $i>2n$. If no component of local dimension $n$ maps to $y$, it vanishes already for $i>2n-1$. If $k(y)$ is finite and $F$ is pure of weight $j$, the degree-$2n$ stalk is pure of weight $2n+j$ when nonzero. This endpoint is attained by $\mathbb P^n\to\Spec\F_q$ with constant coefficient $H^j(E^j)$ for an elliptic curve $E/\F_q$. These assertions do not require the dimension-normalized presentation of $F$.
notes: Any lisse coefficient for vanishing; pure weight-j coefficient at a finite-field point for top weight; no dimension-j normalization required.

statement: The lower-endpoint gate over a trait: Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with finite residue field $k$, fraction field $K$, and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$. Let $\mathcal Z/R$ be regular, proper, flat and generically smooth, with generic fibre $Z$. For $u:\Spec K\hookrightarrow\Spec R$, the assertion that \[ (u_*H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell))_{\bar k} =H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)^{I_K} \quad\text{has weights at most }j \] is equivalent to surjectivity of the specialization map \[ H^j(\mathcal Z_{\bar k},\Q_\ell) \longrightarrow H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)^{I_K}. \] Thus, when $\dim Z=j$, improving the universal $i=0$ coefficient bound from $2j$ to $j$ includes exactly this local invariant cycle assertion.
status: Proved exact equivalence; the general mixed-characteristic vanishing is not asserted
notes: General mixed-characteristic local-invariant-cycle gate remains; abelian-type trait coefficients now satisfy the upper weight-j endpoint unconditionally.

statement: The lower endpoint for abelian-type coefficients: Let $K$ be a complete discretely valued field with finite residue field of characteristic $p$, and let $\ell\ne p$. Suppose that $V$ is the $\ell$-adic realization of a pure weight-$j$ motive which, after a finite extension of $K$, is a direct summand of tensor constructions on the $H^1$ of abelian varieties, their duals and Tate twists. Finite-image Artin factors are allowed. Then the eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius on $V^{I_K}$ have weights at most $j$. In particular this holds for the local realizations of pure absolute-Hodge or motivated motives of abelian type over number fields. The bound is attained for good reduction.
notes: Settles the trait lower endpoint for abelian-type coefficients without the 2026 rationality theorem.

statement: The positive purity range: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a two-dimensional regular local ring of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ and let $U=\Spec R\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$. Every abelian scheme over $U$ extends uniquely over $R$ if $p\notin\mathfrak m^p$. In particular the sufficient absolute ramification bound is $e\leq p-1$, including equality. More generally the same conclusion holds under the complete faithfully flat quotient condition of Vasiu--Zink Theorem 3. If an abelian variety over $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ has good reduction at every height-one prime, these conclusions apply to it. Equivalently, at each such prime one may use the prime-to-residue-characteristic unramifiedness test of the N\'eron--Ogg--Shafarevich criterion.
notes: Improves sufficient e<p-1 to e<=p-1.

statement: An explicit abelian-surface counterexample at $p=2$: Let $k=\overline\F_2$ and \[ R=W(k)[[u,v]]/(2-uv),\qquad K=\operatorname{Frac}(R),\qquad \mathfrak m=(u,v). \] Consider the elliptic schemes \begin{align*} E_1:&\quad Y^2Z+(u+v^2)XYZ+YZ^2=X^3,\\ E_2:&\quad Y^2Z+(v+u^2)XYZ+YZ^2=X^3, \end{align*} with origins $[0:1:0]$, and put $A=E_1\times_R E_2$. The sections \[ P_v=[-v:1:v^3]\in E_1(R),\qquad P_u=[-u:1:u^3]\in E_2(R) \] have order two on the generic fibre. Let $C_K\subset A_K$ be the order-two subgroup generated by $(P_v,P_u)$, and define the abelian surface \[ B_K=A_K/C_K. \] Then $B_K$ has good reduction at every height-one prime of $R$, hence its $T_\ell$ is unramified at every height-one point of $S_\ell=\Spec R[1/\ell]$ for every prime $\ell$, but it does not extend to an abelian scheme over $R$. The schematic closure of $C_K$ in $A$ is explicitly nonflat.
status: Proved refutation of the unrestricted criterion
notes: All polynomial identities checked over integers without inverting 2.

statement: What fails to extend: The abstract finite group $D_U$ already extends as $D$. It is its closed immersion into $A_U$, and consequently the exact sequence defining the isogeny, that cannot extend as a finite flat subgroup. Indeed finite locally free group schemes on a punctured regular local surface extend as objects by extending their coordinate bundles to reflexive modules, which are free in dimension two; multiplication and comultiplication extend by Hartogs. Exactness and closed-immersion conditions need not survive. This is the precise content of the finite-subgroup reduction in R6, rather than a failure to extend the abstract group. The source proof of Vasiu--Zink Lemma 27 reverses the Cartier-dual arrows in its printed embedding sentence; our displayed maps avoid that typing error. Lead C5 is therefore valid as an identification of the extension obstruction, while the unrestricted good-reduction claim is false.
notes: Corrects ambiguity in the finite-subgroup reduction and a dual-arrow typo in Vasiu-Zink Lemma27.

statement: The degree-one and semistable abelian-type cases: Let $K$ be a number field, $v$ a finite place of residue characteristic $p$, and $\ell\ne p$. For $M=h^1(A)$, unramifiedness of $M_\ell$ at $v$ is independent of $\ell$ and is equivalent to good reduction of $A$. It follows for every tensor construction and motivated summand of abelian varieties already having good reduction at $v$. More generally suppose that $A/K$ has semistable reduction at $v$, that its Galois representations take values in its Mumford--Tate group $G$ over $K$, and that a motivated abelian-type object $M$ in the category it generates corresponds to a rational representation $r:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$. Then unramifiedness of $M_\ell$ at $v$ is independent of $\ell\ne p$. The same conclusion holds for potentially CM motives without a semistability assumption.
notes: The elementary cases are now subsumed by c:ell-independence-abelian; retained to isolate the older SGA7/Kisin-Zhou inputs.

statement: A generator with potentially good reduction: Let $M$ be a rational motive of abelian type over a number field $K$, in either the absolute-Hodge or motivated category. Let $v$ have residue characteristic $p$. If $M_{\ell_0}$ is potentially unramified at $v$ for one $\ell_0\ne p$, then, after a finite Galois extension $E/K$, the object $M_E$ belongs to the tensor category generated by finitely many abelian varieties over $E$ which have good reduction at every place above $v$.
notes: Descent via B0 factors; common MT group has finite derived kernel; all places above v retained.

Independence of unramifiedness for all abelian-type motives: Let $M$ be a rational absolute-Hodge or motivated motive of abelian type over a number field $K$, and let $v$ have residue characteristic $p$. If $M_{\ell_0}$ is unramified at $v$ for one $\ell_0
e p$, then $M_\ell$ is unramified at $v$ for every $\ell
e p$. The statement includes $p=2$, and includes $\ell=2$ when $p
