status: Proved, using the October 2026 rationality theorem
notes: Includes arbitrary tensor summands, ramified descent, p=2, and ell=2 when p differs.

statement: The exact role of the new input: The proof does not apply N\'eron--Ogg--Shafarevich to an arbitrary original generator: such a generator need not have good reduction when its summand is unramified. Lemma~\ref{c:potentially-good-generator} changes the generator and proves its potential good reduction. The finite descent action is then recovered over $K$ by the common trace pairing. Since \eqref{c:inertia-graph-lefschetz} is Lefschetz, the proof uses the rationality theorem alone; it does not use the CM Hodge theorem or assume algebraicity of the Hodge projector. It proves independence of unramifiedness and, for potentially unramified objects, independence of the finite inertia character. It does not assert full Weil--Deligne compatibility for objects with nonzero monodromy.
notes: Also gives common finite inertia character for potentially unramified objects; no full nonzero-monodromy WD compatibility claimed.

statement: A purity reduction for homogeneous Chow motives: Let $K$ be a number field, $v$ a finite place with residue field of cardinality $q$, and $p$ its residue characteristic. Let $M=(X,e,m)$ be a rational Chow motive over $K$, where $X$ is smooth projective of dimension $d$ and the rational algebraic projector $e\in\CH^d(X\times_KX)_{\Q}$ acts only in cohomological degree $i$. Suppose that, for one prime $\ell_0\ne p$, the representation $M_{\ell_0}$ is unramified at $v$ and the eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius on it are algebraic numbers all of whose complex conjugates have one common absolute value. Then $M_\ell$ is unramified at $v$ for every $\ell\ne p$. In particular, the asserted independence follows for such a motive if the weight--monodromy conjecture holds for $H^i(X_{\overline{K_v}},\Q_{\ell_0})$: its unramified direct summand $M_{\ell_0}$ is then pure of weight $i-2m$.
notes: Ambient weight-monodromy at the one prime suffices; algebraic projector required.

statement: Exact scope of this reduction: For the full group $H^i(X)$, the purity assumption in the proposition is Serre's unramified-purity conjecture C7 \citep[\S2.3, printed p.~19-07]{c_serre1970local}. For a prescribed proper summand it is the corresponding \emph{motivic extension} of that condition; the literal original C7 must not be silently enlarged. The named weight--monodromy conjecture for the ambient cohomology is a sufficient alternative. The use of Saito's theorem requires an algebraic correspondence. It cannot be applied to an arbitrary absolute-Hodge or motivated projector without an additional comparison result. No converse to any of these named conjectures is proved here, and this proposition does not close the general-motive requirement in C.6.
status: Proved scope clarification; the general claim remains unresolved
notes: No converse to a named conjecture claimed.

statement: The remaining general-motive claim: Theorem~\ref{c:ell-independence-abelian} settles the whole abelian-type assertion, including its finite-inertia descent. The direct argument from an arbitrary original generator would still be invalid: $\bigwedge^2H^1(E)=\Q_\ell(-1)$ is unramified at a place of residue characteristic different from $\ell$, even when $E$ has bad reduction. The weak-lift lemma and the trace argument are what repair that inference. For general motives, the precise named sufficient conjecture is Fontaine's motivic Weil--Deligne compatibility conjecture: \citet[\S2.4.3, Conjecture $C_{\mathrm{WD}}(X,m)$, p.~342, and its motivic formulation in \S2.4.7, pp.~344--345]{c_fontaine1994pst}. The motivic formulation is required to retain the specified projector; compatibility of an unlabelled ambient cohomology representation alone does not identify every prescribed summand. Write the local Weil--Deligne data as $(r_\ell,N_\ell)$, with $r_\ell$ of finite inertial image. On an open subgroup of inertia the actual action is $\exp(t_\ell(\tau)N_\ell)$, where the tame character has infinite image. Consequently \[ M_\ell\text{ is unramified at }v \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_\ell=0\ \text{ and }\ r_\ell|_{I_v}=1. \] Both conditions are invariant under extension of coefficient fields and isomorphism of Weil--Deligne representations. Thus Fontaine's compatibility, which only requires isomorphism after common coefficient extension and not a chosen rational form, implies the requested independence. His weaker monodromy-graded character formulation in \S2.4.5 also suffices: the characters at the identity determine whether the monodromy filtration is concentrated in degree zero, equivalently $N=0$; after that, the finite inertia character detects triviality. This proves an implication, not the exact equivalence requested in the question. Algebraically, the representations trivial on a subgroup $J\subset G$ detect its closed normal closure, not the whole inertia representation. Even all tensor tests do not formally recover the nilpotent's Jordan type: in $\mathfrak{sl}_3$, both $E_{12}$ and $E_{12}+E_{23}$ act nontrivially in every nontrivial algebraic representation, since the differential's kernel is an ideal in the simple Lie algebra. Their ranks differ. The accompanying notes give compatible abstract Weil--Deligne pairs and a matrix certificate; no such pair is asserted to come from a global motive, and it is not a motivic counterexample. The theorem of \citet[Theorem 5.1]{c_commelin2019} concerns abelian motives and quasi-compatibility; by itself it does not supply finite-inertia traces for an arbitrary motive at a bad place. Similarly the $G$-valued expectation of \citet[Conjecture 1.1]{c_kisinzhou2025} is stronger than the asserted triviality test. A proof in the general motivic category, or an exact equivalence with a published named conjecture of precisely the required strength, remains an outstanding assertion, recorded separately from the now proved abelian-type theorem.
status: Unresolved in the general motivic category
notes: Abelian-type gap closed; general exact named-conjecture equivalence remains open in this work. Abstract SL3 examples certify only failure of a formal converse.

statement: Proved: integral finite-modulus Serre group: The fppf quotient $\mathcal G^0=\mathcal T/\mathcal R$ is a separated, flat group scheme of finite type over $\Z$. Its geometric fibres are connected. There is an extension of group schemes \[ 1\longrightarrow\mathcal G^0\longrightarrow\mathcal G \longrightarrow\underline{\Cl^+(k)}\longrightarrow1 \] whose generic fibre is Serre's $S_{\mathfrak m}$ for $\mathfrak m=\prod_{v\text{ real}}v$. In particular $(\mathcal G^0)_\Q=T_{\mathfrak m} =\Res_{k/\Q}\Gm/\overline{E^+}^{\,\mathrm{Zar}}$. The assertion does not say that these integral models are tori at ramified primes or that their representations comprise all CM motives over $k$.
notes: Closure is schematic, not profinite; model need not be a torus at ramified primes.

statement: Refuted literal Frobenius formula; proved correction: The CM type and a uniformizer do not, by the reflex norm alone, determine the Frobenius element of a CM motive. They determine its algebraic Hecke-character part and its principal ideal; the finite-order character data are also required to determine the element.
notes: Counterexample: y^2=x^3-x and y^2=x^3-4x over Q(i), good at5, opposite Frobenius traces.

statement: Refuted: special-fibre gerbe bridge: The proposed morphism from the finite-field motivic gerbe to the special fibre of the integral group in Lead D1 is not a morphism of gerbes over the coefficient field, and good reduction does not make the Frobenius an integral point of that group.
notes: For k=Q the group is Gm and Frobenius p is not in Gm(Z_p); moreover coefficient base Q differs from special-fibre base F_p.

statement: Proved with the stated CM Hodge input: reduction of gerbes: Reduction of CM motives induces a morphism of gerbes over $\Q$ from the abelian motivic gerbe over $\overline\F_p$ to the CM motivic gerbe over $\overline\Q$, bound by $P\to S$. It satisfies the Langlands--Rapoport local conditions. These local conditions alone do not canonically specify its global comparison with a separately chosen pseudomotivic morphism.
status: Proved under stated CM Hodge input (Theorem I of the opened 2026 preprint)
notes: The local conditions alone leave the inverse-limit class-group ambiguity of Milne2003 Thm7.2; no canonical comparison with an unspecified LR representative asserted.

statement: Proved: a power admits an exact-residue-field CM lifting: For every simple abelian variety $A_0/\F_q$ there exist $m\geq1$, a number field $k$, a place $v$ of $k$ with $\kappa(v)=\F_q$, and a CM abelian variety $B/k$, with its full CM field acting over $k$, such that $B$ has good reduction at $v$ and $B_v\sim_{\F_q}A_0^m$. The integer $m$ is not required to equal one.
notes: Independent root audit passed; exact slope convention and number-field full-action conclusion verified in opened primary source.; End0=Q(zeta5); all reflex fields have residueF16. For square use Q(zeta5,sqrt(-3)) and type induced from Q(sqrt(-3)).

statement: Proved: all Weil numbers occur, with variable CM data: Let $\Gamma_q$ be the group of algebraic $p$-units whose complex conjugates have absolute value $q^{w/2}$ for some integer $w$. Every element of $\Gamma_q$ occurs as a Frobenius eigenvalue of the good reduction of a tensor CM motive over some number field at a place with residue field $\F_q$. Every integral weight-one member already occurs in $H^1$ of a CM abelian variety with such reduction. No single number field, finite modulus, or primitive CM type is asserted to work for all members.
notes: Varying number field and CM data is essential. The exponent m is unrestricted; this does not claim simple isogeny classes themselves always lift.

statement: Proved: D.2(a) for abelian type and its general equivalent: For a motive $M$ of abelian type, in either category, \[ G_{\mathrm{mot}}(M)^\circ\text{ is commutative} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad M\in\CM(k). \] For arbitrary motives the same classification is equivalent to the following restricted Hodge-class assertion: \emph{CM comparison case of the absolute-Hodge (respectively motivated Hodge) conjecture.} If $G_{\mathrm{mot}}(M)^\circ$ is commutative and $N$ is a CM abelian motive over $\overline k$, every rational Hodge morphism $H_B(M_{\overline k})\to H_B(N)$ is induced by an absolute Hodge (respectively motivated) correspondence. It is enough in this assertion to require one Hodge isomorphism to some such $N$ to lift. In the absolute-Hodge case this is a precise restriction of \citet[Conjecture 8.24]{c_delignehodge1982}, rather than a claim of equivalence with the unrestricted conjecture.
notes: Full faithfulness, CM Hodge category, finite descent and induction are supplied.; This is the general-case output explicitly allowed by the question. It is not the unrestricted Hodge conjecture and is not implied by CM Hodge classes alone.; Potentially CM + Artin is correct Taniyama category, not all quotient groups are metabelian.

statement: Refuted: metabelian motives are all Taniyama quotients: The category of Taniyama quotients is $\CM(\Q)$ and contains motives with non-metabelian Galois group. Its metabelian objects are precisely the representations of the maximal metabelian quotient of the Taniyama group. Among motives of abelian type, this is exactly the category with metabelian motivic Galois group.
notes: h0(Spec Q(alpha)), alpha^4-alpha-1=0, has group S4, a nonmetabelian Taniyama quotient. Correct metabelian category is Rep(T/closed T-second-derived), within CM motives.; Potentially CM + Artin is correct Taniyama category, not all quotient groups are metabelian.

statement: Known and rechecked: the Taniyama comparison: The two Betti fibre functors on geometric CM motives at $\widetilde\xi$ and $\widetilde\xi'=\sigma\widetilde\xi$ are related by the fibre of the Taniyama group above $\sigma|_{\overline\Q}$. Their Hodge types change by the $\Aut(\C)$ action and their finite-adelic comparison is supplied by its canonical adelic section. Formula~\eqref{eq:d-conjugate-cm-type} gives the explicit CM-type and polarization change.
notes: No canonical rational Hodge isomorphism is falsely asserted; explicit lattice and polarization formula is included.; The cover reading metabeliens cannot be visually confirmed because scans were not supplied; its naive group-theoretic slogan is refuted by D.2.b.; Potentially CM + Artin is correct Taniyama category, not all quotient groups are metabelian.

statement: Proved: finite-place kernel and fibre functors: There is a canonical identification \[ \Sha^1_f(\Q,S^K) \simeq \left\{(\epsilon_v)_{v\mid\infty}\in\F_2^r: \sum_v\epsilon_v=0\right\}. \] For the geometric neutral category of CM motives whose CM fields are subfields of $K$, with Betti functor as origin, this group classifies the isomorphism classes of rational fibre functors that become isomorphic to Betti at every finite completion. It has $2^{r-1}$ elements. Thus finite comparisons single out Betti only when $r=1$. Adding a real comparison singles it out for every $r$.
notes: All-places kernel is zero; finite-place kernel has 2^(r-1) elements.; Arithmetic Artin data and smaller subcategories require their actual group and cannot silently be replaced by S^K.; It is unique iff [K+:Q]=1; F=Q(sqrt5), K=F(i) gives the nontrivial class (-1,-1)_F.; Computed actual S^K cohomology, not merely the norm-one torus.

statement: Verified: a non-Betti form with all finite comparisons: Take $F=\Q(\sqrt5)$ and $K=F(i)$. The quaternion algebra $(-1,-1)_F$ is nonsplit at both real embeddings. It is split at every finite place: over $\Q$ Hamilton's algebra is ramified only at $2$ and infinity, and $2$ is inert in $F$ because $x^2-x-1$ is irreducible modulo two. The degree-two local extension at $2$ multiplies the invariant $1/2$ by two. The algebra is split by $K$, and its corestriction to $\Q$ is trivial since its two real invariants sum to zero in $\Q/\Z$. It is the nonzero element of $\Sha^1_f(\Q,S^K)\simeq\Z/2$. Equivalently, the corresponding $U$-torsor is $x^2+y^2=-1$ over $F$. Twisting Betti by its lift to an $S^K$-torsor supplies the asserted different rational fibre functor. The irreducibility calculation is recorded in the program.
notes: It is unique iff [K+:Q]=1; F=Q(sqrt5), K=F(i) gives the nontrivial class (-1,-1)_F.; Computed actual S^K cohomology, not merely the norm-one torus.

statement: Proved: the complete lattice and rank answer to 15:151: The image $I_\Sigma$ of $\psi_\Sigma$ is the connected $\Q$-torus with character and cocharacter lattices \begin{align*} X^*(I_\Sigma)&=\Z^{I_E}/\ker(A^{\mathsf t}) \simeq\im(A^{\mathsf t})\subset\Z^{I_K},\\ X_*(I_\Sigma)&=(\im A\otimes\Q)\cap\Z^{I_E}. \end{align*} In particular $\dim I_\Sigma=\operatorname{rank}_\Q(A)$. If $E$ is CM of degree $2g$, put \[ C_E=\{x\in\Res_{E/\Q}\Gm: x\overline x\in\Gm\subset\Res_{E^+/\Q}\Gm\}. \] Then $I_\Sigma\subset C_E$, and the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $I_\Sigma=C_E$; \item $\operatorname{rank}_\Q(A)=g+1$; \item every rational row relation of $A$ is generated by $e_\sigma+e_{c\sigma}-e_\tau-e_{c\tau}$. \end{enumerate} These are effective necessary and sufficient conditions for every CM type, including non-Galois and imprimitive types. For the CM type $\Phi$ represented by $\Sigma$, $I_\Sigma=\MT(E,\Phi)$.
notes: Cocharacter saturation is necessary; full norm-compatible torus iff rank=g+1, equivalently only pair-sum row relations.; No nondegeneracy hypothesis.; Fixed finite-modulus quotient may have extra finite unit quotient and need only be isogenous to the standard connected Serre torus.

statement: Proved: the compact part in the manuscript's reduction: Let $V'_K=\ker(N_{K/\Q}:S^K\to\Gm)$, and let $\nu:C_E\to\Gm$ send $x$ to its common product $x_\sigma x_{c\sigma}$. Then \[ \psi_\Sigma(V'_K)=I_\Sigma\cap\ker\nu,\qquad \dim\psi_\Sigma(V'_K)=\operatorname{rank}_\Q A-1, \] and the character lattice of this image is \[ \im(A^{\mathsf t})/\Z\mathbf1_{I_K}. \] The image is all of the norm-one torus of $E/E^+$ precisely when $\operatorname{rank}_\Q A=g+1$.
notes: The scalar and compact factors intersect in mu2; no false integral direct-product decomposition.
